claims.statement: Ved-ava, also called Vedmastor-ava ("water-mother") or Ved-azěrava ("water-hostess"), is a water and fertility deity shared by several fishing Finno-Ugric peoples; among the Mordvins (in what is now western Russia) she was the Water Mother, ruler of the waters and their bounty and an important fertility deity.
claims.statement_id: Ved-ava, juga disebut Vedmastor-ava ("ibu air") atau Ved-azěrava ("nyonya air"), adalah dewi air dan kesuburan yang dikenal beberapa bangsa Fino-Ugria yang hidup dari menangkap ikan; bagi orang Mordvin (wilayah yang kini Rusia barat) ia Ibu Air, penguasa perairan dan hasilnya, sekaligus dewi kesuburan penting.
claims.quote: Ved-ava, also called Vedmastor-ava (water-mother) or Ved-azěrava (water-hostess) is a water and fertility deity, common to several Finno-Ugric peoples traditionally dependent on fishing. Among the Mordvins (an area in what is now Western Russia) she was the Water Mother, ruler of the waters and their bounty, as well as an important fertility deity.

claims.statement: She is generally depicted as a mermaid-like water creature with long hair, large breasts and a fish's lower body with tail, sometimes playing music or singing to seduce people.
claims.statement_id: Ia umumnya digambarkan sebagai makhluk air mirip putri duyung berambut panjang, berpayudara besar, dan bertubuh bawah ikan berekor, yang kadang memainkan musik atau bernyanyi untuk memikat manusia.
claims.quote: She is generally depicted as a water creature resembling a mermaid, with long hair, large breasts, and the lower body of a fish complete with tail, and is sometimes said to play or sing, seducing humans with her music.

claims.statement: Fishermen offered her the first of their catch and kept many taboos about her while fishing; she was originally mainly a fertility goddess, her mermaid form and link with drowning coming later.
claims.statement_id: Para nelayan mempersembahkan tangkapan pertama kepadanya dan mematuhi banyak pantangan terkait dirinya saat menangkap ikan; semula ia terutama dewi kesuburan, sedangkan wujud putri duyung dan kaitannya dengan orang tenggelam muncul belakangan.
claims.quote: Fishermen sacrificed to her the first of their catch and observed numerous taboos related to her while fishing. She was originally mainly a fertility goddess, with her form as a mermaid and association with drowning coming later.

claims.statement: In Mordvin tradition she protected marriage, childbirth, love and fertility; young couples hoping for children prayed to her, and infertility was often blamed on her anger.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Mordvin ia pelindung pernikahan, persalinan, cinta, dan kesuburan; pasangan muda yang ingin punya anak berdoa kepadanya, dan kemandulan sering dianggap akibat kemarahannya.
claims.quote: In Mordvin tradition, she was the protector of marriage, childbirth, love, and fertility. Young couples hoping to have children would pray to her, and infertility was often ascribed to her being angry with whomever was suffering it.

claims.statement: Ved-ava, known as Veden Emo or Veen Emo in Finnish mythology, Veteema in Estonian and Wedhen Eme or Veden Emä in Karelian, is considered a goddess of the waters.
claims.statement_id: Ved-ava, yang dikenal sebagai Veden Emo atau Veen Emo dalam mitologi Finlandia, Veteema dalam mitologi Estonia, dan Wedhen Eme atau Veden Emä dalam mitologi Karelia, dianggap dewi perairan.
claims.quote: Ved-ava (conosciuta come Veden Emo oppure Veen Emo nella mitologia finlandese, Veteema nella mitologia estone e Wedhen Eme oppure Veden Emä in quella careliana è considerata una divinità delle acque.

claims.statement: A sailors' superstition said that seeing her brought illness and scurvy.
claims.statement_id: Menurut takhayul pelaut, melihatnya membawa penyakit dan sariawan (skorbut).
claims.quote: Una superstizione dei marinari diceva che vederla portava malattie e scorbuto.

claims.statement: A person who sees Vediava falls ill and often drowns; these deities are often associated with drowning.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang melihat Vediava jatuh sakit dan sering tenggelam; dewi-dewi ini kerap dikaitkan dengan orang tenggelam.
claims.quote: Pamačius Vediavą žmogus suserga, dažnai paskęsta. Šios dievybės dažnai siejamos su skendimu.

claims.statement: Zheuzhyk is a creature of Belarusian mythology, a good being living deep in the lake bed and regarded as the guardian of the rivers and lakes of Belarus.
claims.statement_id: Zheuzhyk adalah makhluk mitologi Belarus yang baik hati, tinggal jauh di dasar danau, dan dianggap penjaga sungai dan danau di Belarus.
claims.quote: is a creature of Belarusian mythology. It is considered to be a good creature that lives deeply in the lake bed. Zheuzhyk is considered to be the guardian of rivers and lakes of Belarus.

claims.statement: In Belarusian folklore Zheuzhyk is described as a thin old man with a long red beard and long, thin arms and legs.
claims.statement_id: Dalam folklor Belarus, Zheuzhyk digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua kurus berjanggut merah panjang dengan lengan dan kaki panjang dan kurus.
claims.quote: In Belarusian folklore Zheuzhyk is described as a thin old man with a long red beard, long and thin arms and legs.

claims.statement: By day Zheuzhyk swims underwater, and by night slowly rounds his domain by boat, parting the waves; it is believed that if someone gets into trouble on the water Zheuzhyk will surely come to the rescue, and he is so strong he can even stop wind and storm.
claims.statement_id: Pada siang hari Zheuzhyk berenang di bawah air dan pada malam hari mengelilingi wilayahnya dengan perahu sambil membelah ombak; dipercaya bila seseorang mendapat kesulitan di air, Zheuzhyk pasti datang menolong, dan ia begitu kuat hingga bisa menghentikan angin dan badai.
claims.quote: As it is said in Belarusian myths, during a day Zheuzhyk swims underwater, and at night Zheuzhyk slowly swims round its possession on boat, dispersing the waves. There is a belief, that is somebody gets into a trouble on water, Zheuzhyk will surely come to rescue. Zheuzhyk is so strong that it may even stop the wind and the storm.

claims.statement: As an ancient Belarusian patron of rivers or water deity, Zheuzhyk was described, and probably invented, by the folklorist Pavel Shpilevsky (Drevlyansky).
claims.statement_id: Sebagai pelindung sungai atau dewa air Belarus kuno, Zheuzhyk digambarkan, dan kemungkinan dikarang, oleh folkloris Pavel Shpilevsky (Drevlyansky).
claims.quote: Как древнебелорусский покровитель рек или водяное божество описан (и, вероятно, придуман) фольклористом Павлом Шпилевским (Древлянским).

claims.statement: All water spirits obey Zheuzhyk, including the Vadavik and Lazavik.
claims.statement_id: Semua roh air tunduk kepada Zheuzhyk, termasuk Vadavik dan Lazavik.
claims.quote: Жэўжыку падпарадкоўваюцца ўсе вадзяныя духі, у тым ліку Вадавік і Лазавік.

claims.statement: In Belarusian sayings, "What a Zheuzhyk!" means how nimble, and "Dives like Zheuzhyk" means swims like Zheuzhyk.
claims.statement_id: Dalam peribahasa Belarus, "Seperti Zheuzhyk!" berarti betapa cekatan, dan "Menyelam seperti Zheuzhyk" berarti berenang seperti Zheuzhyk.
claims.quote: «Які Жэўжык» — які спрытны! «Бы Жэўжык нырае» — нібы Жэўжык плавае;

claims.statement: There is a sculpture of Zheuzhyk by the Belarusian sculptor Anton Shipitsa based on illustrations by Valery Slauk.
claims.statement_id: Terdapat patung Zheuzhyk karya pematung Belarus Anton Shipitsa berdasarkan ilustrasi Valery Slauk.
claims.quote: Sculpture of Zheuzhyk, by Belarusian sculptor Anton Shipitsa on the basis of illustrations of Valery Slauk

claims.statement: Zhytsen or Žycień is a benevolent creature of Belarusian mythology said to live in fields; the name literally means "rye creature", from Belarusian zhyta, "rye".
claims.statement_id: Zhytsen atau Žycień adalah makhluk baik dalam mitologi Belarus yang konon tinggal di ladang; namanya secara harfiah berarti "makhluk gandum hitam", dari kata Belarus zhyta, "gandum hitam".
claims.quote: is a positive creature from Belarusian mythology said to live in fields. The name literally means "rye creature", from Belarusian жыта, "rye".

claims.statement: Zhytsen is often called a spirit of wealth and wellbeing; it is believed to help crops and vegetables ripen well and so is considered the caretaker of good harvests.
claims.statement_id: Zhytsen sering disebut roh kekayaan dan kesejahteraan; ia dipercaya membantu tanaman dan sayuran matang dengan baik, sehingga dianggap pengurus panen yang baik.
claims.quote: Zhyten is often called a spirit of wealth and wellbeing. It is believed that Zhytsen contributes to good ripening of crops and vegetables, and accordingly, Zhyten is considered the caretaker of good harvests.

claims.statement: Zhytsen walks the fields making sure the crops are well reaped; Belarusian folklore holds that if it finds ears of grain left behind, it binds them into sheaves and carries them to the fields of more diligent farmers.
claims.statement_id: Zhytsen berjalan melintasi ladang memastikan panen dituai dengan baik; dalam folklor Belarus dipercaya bila ia menemukan bulir yang tertinggal, ia mengikatnya menjadi berkas dan membawanya ke ladang petani yang lebih rajin.
claims.quote: Zhytsen walks through the fields and ensures that crops there are well reaped. It is believed in Belarusian folklore that if Zhytsen finds some left ears of grain, it binds them in sheaves and brings to the fields of more diligent farmers.

claims.statement: As an ancient Belarusian god of fertility and autumn, Zhytsen was described, and probably invented, by the folklorist Pavel Shpilevsky (Drevlyansky).
claims.statement_id: Sebagai dewa kesuburan dan musim gugur Belarus kuno, Zhytsen digambarkan, dan kemungkinan dikarang, oleh folkloris Pavel Shpilevsky (Drevlyansky).
claims.quote: Как древнебелорусский бог плодородия и осени описан (и, вероятно, придуман) фольклористом Павлом Шпилевским (Древлянским).

claims.statement: A peculiarity of Zhytsen is a third eye on the back of the head, which helps it do its work better.
claims.statement_id: Ciri khas Zhytsen adalah mata ketiga di tengkuk, yang membantunya menjalankan tugasnya dengan lebih baik.
claims.quote: Особенностью Житеня является третий глаз на затылке, который нужен для лучшего выполнения задач этого мифологического персонажа.

claims.statement: In Belarus Zhytsen was imagined as a little old man ("Rye Grandfather") with a long beard.
claims.statement_id: Di Belarus, Zhytsen dibayangkan sebagai kakek kecil ("Kakek Gandum Hitam") berjanggut panjang.
claims.quote: На Беларусі Жыценя уяўлялі маленькім дзедам («Жытні дзед») з доўгай барадой.

claims.statement: The figure of Zhytsen still appears in Belarusian folklore, for example in the saying "Zhytsen gave bread".
claims.statement_id: Sosok Zhytsen masih tampak dalam folklor Belarus, antara lain dalam ungkapan "Zhytsen memberi roti".
claims.quote: Образ Жиценя й досі спостерігається в білоруському фольклорі, зокрема в примовці «Жыцень хлеба дав».

claims.statement: Błędnica is a forest demoness said to lead people astray, leaving her victims alone deep in the forest to starve or be eaten by wild animals; this evil being is most often described as a pretty young girl.
claims.statement_id: Błędnica adalah demon perempuan hutan yang konon menyesatkan orang dan meninggalkan korbannya sendirian di kedalaman hutan hingga mati kelaparan atau dimangsa binatang buas; makhluk jahat ini paling sering digambarkan sebagai gadis muda yang cantik.
claims.quote: – a forest demoness, which is said to have led people astray, leaving its victims alone in the depths of the forest to die of starvation or to be eaten by wild animals. The evil entity is most often described as a young and pretty girl.

claims.statement: It is believed the only way to drive the demon away was with strong spells or by making an offering, either at home or during the hunt.
claims.statement_id: Dipercaya satu-satunya cara mengusir demon ini adalah dengan mantra yang kuat atau dengan mempersembahkan sesuatu, baik di rumah maupun saat berburu.
claims.quote: It is believed that the only way to chase the demon away was to use some strong spells or to sacrifice something either at one's home or during the hunt.

claims.statement: The barstuk is a kind of small dwarf of Warmian-Masurian folk tales that lived in forests and is believed to have helped people whose houses it secretly visited.
claims.statement_id: Barstuk adalah sejenis kurcaci kecil dalam cerita rakyat Warmia-Masuria yang menghuni hutan dan dipercaya menolong orang yang rumahnya ia kunjungi diam-diam.
claims.quote: Barstuk is a type of small dwarf in Warmian-Masurian folk tales. The creature inhabited forests and it is believed to have been helping people whose houses it secretly visited.

claims.statement: According to Louis Noirot, the barstuk is a Prussian deity later identified as a kind of dwarf in the folk tales of the Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship in Poland.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Louis Noirot, barstuk adalah dewa Prusia yang kemudian dianggap sejenis kurcaci dalam cerita rakyat Provinsi Warmia-Masuria di Polandia.
claims.quote: Un Barstuk est, selon Louis Noirot, une divinité prusse, identifiée ultérieurement comme un type de nain présents dans les contes folkloriques du voïvodie de Varmie-Mazurie en Pologne.

claims.statement: Dziwożona (or Mamuna or Boginka) is a malicious, dangerous female swamp demon of Slavic mythology; those thought most likely to become one after death were midwives, old maids, unmarried mothers, pregnant women who died before childbirth, and abandoned children born out of wedlock.
claims.statement_id: Dziwożona (juga Mamuna atau Boginka) adalah demon rawa perempuan dalam mitologi Slavia yang jahat dan berbahaya; yang paling berisiko menjadi demon ini setelah mati adalah bidan, perawan tua, ibu yang tidak menikah, perempuan hamil yang meninggal sebelum melahirkan, dan anak haram yang ditelantarkan.
claims.quote: Dziwożona (or Mamuna or Boginka) is a female swamp demon in Slavic mythology known for being malicious and dangerous. Most at risk of becoming one of these demons after death were thought to be midwives, old maids, unmarried mothers, pregnant women who die before childbirth, as well as abandoned children born out of wedlock.

claims.statement: In Slovak she was called "diva lena" or "divá žena", in Czech "divoženka", meaning "wild woman".
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Slowakia ia disebut "diva lena" atau "divá žena", dan dalam bahasa Ceko "divoženka", yang berarti "perempuan liar".
claims.quote: In Slovak she was called „diva lena”/ „divá žena”, in Czech „divoženka”, which means "wild woman".

claims.statement: Dziwożona was said to live in thickets near rivers, streams and lakes; some said she was an ugly old woman with a hairy body, long straight hair and breasts so huge she used them to wash her clothes, wearing a red hat with a fern twig.
claims.statement_id: Dziwożona konon tinggal di semak dekat sungai, anak sungai, dan danau; menurut sebagian orang ia berwujud perempuan tua buruk rupa bertubuh berbulu, berambut panjang lurus, dan berpayudara begitu besar hingga dipakai mencuci pakaian, serta memakai topi merah berhias ranting pakis.
claims.quote: Dziwożona was said to live in thickets near rivers, streams and lakes. According to some, she took the form of an ugly, old woman with a hairy body, long straight hair and breasts so huge that she used them to wash her clothes. On her head she wore a red hat with a fern twig attached to it.

claims.statement: Dziwożona was said to kidnap human babies right after birth and replace them with her own children, known as changelings.
claims.statement_id: Dziwożona konon menculik bayi manusia segera setelah lahir dan menggantinya dengan anaknya sendiri, yang disebut anak tukaran (changeling).
claims.quote: Dziwożona was said to kidnap human babies just after they were born and replace them with her own children, known as foundlings or changelings.

claims.statement: To protect a child from Dziwożona, a mother had to tie a red ribbon round its hand (a custom still kept in some regions of Poland without its original meaning), put a red hat on its head and shield its face from moonlight.
claims.statement_id: Untuk melindungi anak dari Dziwożona, ibu harus mengikat pita merah di tangannya (kebiasaan yang masih bertahan di beberapa daerah Polandia tanpa makna aslinya), memakaikan topi merah, dan melindungi wajahnya dari cahaya bulan.
claims.quote: To protect a child against being kidnapped by Dziwożona, a mother had to tie a red ribbon around its hand (this custom is still preserved in some regions of Poland, although without the original meaning), put a red hat on its head and shield its face from the light of the moon.

claims.statement: To get her baby back, the mother had to take the changeling to a midden, whip it with a birch twig and pour water on it from an eggshell, shouting "Take yours, give mine back!", whereupon Dziwożona usually pitied her offspring, took it away and returned the stolen child.
claims.statement_id: Untuk mendapatkan bayinya kembali, ibu harus membawa anak tukaran ke tumpukan sampah, memukulnya dengan ranting birch, dan menyiramnya dengan air dari cangkang telur sambil berteriak "Ambil milikmu, kembalikan milikku!", lalu Dziwożona biasanya merasa iba pada anaknya, mengambilnya, dan mengembalikan bayi yang dicuri.
claims.quote: The mother had to take the changeling to a midden, whip it with a birch twig and pour water over it from an eggshell, shouting "Take yours, give mine back!", at which point Dziwożona normally felt sorry for her offspring and took it away, returning the one she stole.

claims.statement: The word "dziwożona" ("wild woman") is a Polish loan from Slovak, popularised by Zygmunt Kaczkowski's novel "Dziwożona", published in 1855.
claims.statement_id: Kata "dziwożona" ("perempuan liar") adalah pinjaman bahasa Polandia dari bahasa Slowakia, dan dipopulerkan oleh novel "Dziwożona" karya Zygmunt Kaczkowski yang terbit tahun 1855.
claims.quote: Wyraz „dziwożona” (dzika żona/kobieta) jest w języku polskim pożyczką z języka słowackiego: „diva lena”/ „divá žena” oznaczała „dziką kobietę”, a polski odpowiednik spopularyzowany został przez wydaną w 1855 powieść „Dziwożona” autorstwa Zygmunta Kaczkowskiego.

claims.statement: The word "dziwożona" was used especially among the Tatra highlanders.
claims.statement_id: Kata "dziwożona" terutama dipakai di kalangan penduduk pegunungan Tatra.
claims.quote: Wyraz „dziwożona” szczególnie stosowany był u górali tatrzańskich

claims.statement: A fext is a mythical undead creature of Slavic mythology whose origins lie in the terrors of the Thirty Years' War (17th century) in central Europe.
claims.statement_id: Fext adalah makhluk mayat hidup mitos dalam mitologi Slavia yang asal-usulnya berkaitan dengan kengerian Perang Tiga Puluh Tahun (abad ke-17) di Eropa Tengah.
claims.quote: A Fext is a mythical undead creature in Slavic mythology. Its origins are found in the terrors of the Thirty Years' War (17th century) in central Europe.

claims.statement: The fext is said to be invulnerable to bullets except those made of glass, and some great generals of the time were called fexts because of their supposed immortality.
claims.statement_id: Konon fext kebal terhadap peluru, kecuali peluru dari kaca, dan beberapa jenderal besar masa itu dijuluki fext karena dianggap tak bisa mati.
claims.quote: It is said that the Fext is invincible to bullets, except bullets made of glass. Some of the great generals of that time were called Fexts because of their assumed immortality.

claims.statement: Fext (also fekst or fest, probably from German fest, "firm", for its invulnerability) is a folk term for a person whose remains did not decay after death but merely dried and stayed intact.
claims.statement_id: Fext (juga fekst atau fest, mungkin dari kata Jerman fest, "kokoh", karena kekebalannya) adalah sebutan rakyat bagi orang yang jasadnya tidak membusuk setelah mati, hanya mengering dan tetap utuh.
claims.quote: Fext (též fekst či fest, asi z německého fest, pevný, podle nezranitelnosti) je lidové označení pro člověka, jehož ostatky se po smrti nerozložily, jen seschly a setrvávaly v neporušené podobě.

claims.statement: Oral tradition often credited fexts with supernatural powers they already had in life, usually invulnerability; legends of fexts mostly came from the Rychnov region and its surroundings.
claims.statement_id: Tradisi lisan sering memberi fext kemampuan gaib yang sudah dimiliki semasa hidup, biasanya kekebalan; legenda tentang fext umumnya berasal dari daerah Rychnov dan sekitarnya.
claims.quote: Lidová slovesnost často fextům připisovala nadpřirozené schopnosti, kterými měli disponovat již za svého života, zpravidla to byla nezranitelnost. Pověsti o fextech pocházely obvykle z Rychnovska a okolí.

claims.statement: According to the accounts of Mrs Luňáčková and Fr. Malátek of Velká Skrovnice, a fext was born in a double caul: one was burned after birth, the other rolled up and sewn under the newborn's arm.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kesaksian Ibu Luňáčková dan Fr. Malátek dari Velká Skrovnice, fext lahir dengan selaput ganda: satu dibakar setelah kelahiran, yang lain digulung dan dijahitkan di bawah ketiak bayi.
claims.quote: Podle výpovědí paní Luňáčkové a Fr. Malátka z Velké Skrovnice přišel fext na svět ve dvojím obalu. Jeden byl po narození spálen, druhý sbalen do klubíčka a zašit novorozeněti pod paži.

claims.statement: It was also said, however, that invulnerability was gained through some spell or by signing one's soul over to the devil.
claims.statement_id: Namun dikatakan pula bahwa kekebalan itu diperoleh dengan sihir atau dengan menjual jiwa kepada setan.
claims.quote: Také se ale říkalo, že nezranitelnosti bylo dosaženo nějakým kouzlem nebo upsáním duše ďáblovi.

claims.statement: Legends of fexts are known in Europe only among Czechs (and Slovaks), Germans and Swedes, which may relate to the myth's origin in the Thirty Years' War.
claims.statement_id: Legenda tentang fext di Eropa hanya dikenal oleh orang Ceko (dan Slowakia), Jerman, dan Swedia, yang mungkin berkaitan dengan munculnya mitos ini pada masa Perang Tiga Puluh Tahun.
claims.quote: Zajímavé je, že pověsti o fextech znají v Evropě jen Češi (+ Slováci), Němci a Švédové. Může to souviset se vznikem tohoto mýtu v dobách třicetileté vál

claims.statement: The firefox (tulikettu, tulirepo or tulikko) is a mythical creature of the folklore of northern and eastern Finland, a fox whose tail sparkles with fire.
claims.statement_id: Rubah Api (tulikettu, tulirepo, atau tulikko) adalah makhluk mitos dalam cerita rakyat Finlandia utara dan timur, seekor rubah yang ekornya memercikkan api.
claims.quote: Firefox (tulikettu or tulirepo or tulikko) is a mythical creature in the folklore of northern and eastern Finland. It is a fox whose tail twinkles fire.

claims.statement: According to folk stories the firefox lives far off in woodland hideouts or in the north, and very few have seen it; it is black by day but sparkles with fire by night.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat, Rubah Api tinggal jauh di tempat persembunyian di hutan atau di utara dan sangat sedikit yang pernah melihatnya; pada siang hari ia hitam, tetapi pada malam hari memercikkan api.
claims.quote: According to folk stories, the Firefox lives far away in hideouts in the woods, or in the north, and very few are said to have seen it. Firefox is black during days but twinkles fire during nights.

claims.statement: According to stories, firefox hide was used to light gunpowder stores at night instead of dangerous open flame; the hide was considered immensely valuable, and hunters dream of the firefox, since catching it is said to make a hunter rich for life.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita, kulit Rubah Api dipakai menerangi gudang mesiu pada malam hari sebagai pengganti api terbuka yang berbahaya; kulitnya dianggap sangat berharga, dan pemburu memimpikannya karena konon menangkapnya membuat pemburu kaya seumur hidup.
claims.quote: According to stories, the leather of a Firefox has been used to illuminate powder storages at nights instead of dangerous open fire. The leather of a Firefox has been considered as immensely valuable. Hunters dream of the Firefox, since it has been said that catching it makes the hunter rich for the rest of his life.

claims.statement: The firefox gave its name to the northern lights, called "fox's fires" (revontulet) in Finnish; in Lapland it is told that its tail throws sparks when it brushes low branches or bushes as it runs, causing the northern lights.
claims.statement_id: Rubah Api memberi nama bagi cahaya utara (aurora), yang dalam bahasa Finlandia disebut "api rubah" (revontulet); di Lapland diceritakan bahwa ekornya memercikkan bunga api saat menyentuh dahan rendah atau semak ketika berlari, sehingga menimbulkan cahaya utara.
claims.quote: Firefox has given its name for northern lights which are called "fox's fires" (revontulet) in the Finnish language. In Lapland it has been told that the Firefox causes the northern lights with its tail which flings sparks when it touches low hanging branches or bushes while the fox is running.

claims.statement: On 12 December 2025 NASA published a photo of a wild fox under the northern lights as its Astronomy Picture of the Day, taken by Dennis Lehtonen in Kilpisjärvi, Finland, referencing Finnish mythology in the caption.
claims.statement_id: Pada 12 Desember 2025 NASA menerbitkan foto rubah liar di bawah cahaya utara sebagai Astronomy Picture of the Day, karya fotografer Dennis Lehtonen di Kilpisjärvi, Finlandia, dengan rujukan ke mitologi Finlandia dalam keterangannya.
claims.quote: On December 12, 2025, NASA published a photograph of a wild fox under the northern lights as their Astronomy Picture of the Day, taken by photographer Dennis Lehtonen in Kilpisjärvi, Finland, and referencing Finnish mythology in the description.

claims.statement: The Lithuanian article likewise calls Ugninė lapė (Firefox) a mythical creature of northern and eastern Finnish folklore, imagined as a fox whose tail glows with fire.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Lituania juga menyebut Ugninė lapė (Rubah Api) sebagai makhluk mitos dalam folklor Finlandia utara dan timur, dibayangkan sebagai rubah dengan ekor yang berkilau api.
claims.quote: Ugninė lapė (suom. tulikettu ar tulirepo, tulikko) – mitinė būtybė, minima šiaurinės ir rytinės Suomijos tautosakoje. Įsivaizduojama kaip lapė, kurios uodega žėri ugnimi.

claims.statement: Gulyabani (Azerbaijani Qulyabani, "werewolf"; from Arabic ghul, "monster-demon", and Persian yaban, "desert") is a shapeshifter, a lesser evil spirit in the beliefs of the Azerbaijanis, Turks, Kyrgyz and Tajiks.
claims.statement_id: Gulyabani (bahasa Azerbaijan Qulyabani, "manusia jadi-jadian"; dari bahasa Arab ghul, "monster-demon", dan bahasa Persia yaban, "padang gurun") adalah makhluk pengubah wujud, roh jahat rendahan dalam kepercayaan orang Azerbaijan, Turki, Kirgiz, dan Tajik.
claims.quote: (азерб. Qulyabani — «оборотень», с араб. гул — «чудовище-демон», с перс. ябан — «пустыня») — оборотень, низший злой дух в представлении азербайджанцев (гул-ябаны, гули-ябаны, биабан-гули), турок, киргизов (гульбиябан), таджиков (гул, гул-ёвони).

claims.statement: According to Azerbaijanis and Turks, the gulyabani was an evil spirit living in the steppe or a cemetery, also met in underground places, ruins and old battlefields; its favourite pastime was frightening belated night travellers and caravan wanderers.
claims.statement_id: Menurut orang Azerbaijan dan Turki, gulyabani adalah roh jahat yang tinggal di stepa atau pemakaman, juga bisa ditemui di ruang bawah tanah, reruntuhan, dan bekas medan perang; kegemarannya menakut-nakuti pengembara malam yang terlambat dan anggota kafilah.
claims.quote: По представлениям азербайджанцев и турок, гульябани был злым духом, жившим в степи или на кладбище. Его также можно было встретить в подземельях, руинах, на местах битв и побоищ. Излюбленным его занятием было пугать припозднившихся ночных путников, странников из караванов.

claims.statement: In Azerbaijani belief the gulyabani had werewolf traits, liking to ride horses at night and tangle their manes; if caught and a needle stuck in the collar of its clothes, it would work like a slave ("gul" in Azerbaijani means "slave"), but would carry out all its master's orders backwards.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan Azerbaijan, gulyabani bersifat seperti manusia jadi-jadian yang pada malam hari suka menunggang kuda dan mengusutkan surainya; bila ditangkap dan jarum ditancapkan di kerah pakaiannya, ia akan bekerja seperti budak ("gul" dalam bahasa Azerbaijan berarti "budak"), tetapi semua perintah tuannya akan ia kerjakan terbalik.
claims.quote: Согласно поверьям азербайджанцев, гульябани имел черты оборотня, который по ночам любил ездить на лошади, запутывать ей гриву. По поверью если его поймать и воткнуть в ворот его одежды иголку, он, подобно рабу («гул» в переводе с азербайджанского означает «раб»), станет работать на человека. Но все приказы хозяина он будет выполнять наоборот.

claims.statement: According to the Azerbaijani article, its counterpart Quyux means a wild being; in the best-known description it appears in the dark in the steppes and cemeteries, its body covered in yellowish-red hair, foul-smelling and very large.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel Azerbaijan, padanannya Quyux berarti makhluk liar; menurut gambaran paling terkenal ia muncul dalam gelap di padang dan pemakaman, tubuhnya tertutup bulu kuning kemerahan, berbau busuk, dan sangat besar.
claims.quote: Quyux, vəhşi varlıq deməkdir. Ən məşhur təsvirə görə, qaranlıqda çöllərdə və qəbiristanlıqlarda ortaya çıxır. Bədəni sarı qırmızı tüklə örtülü, pis qoxuludur. Çox iridir.

claims.statement: In Azerbaijani mythology Qulyabanı (from Persian ghoul-e yabani or ghoul-e biyabani, "wild giant" or "giant of the plains") is a wild beast, an extraordinary, predatory, hairy being.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Azerbaijan, Qulyabanı (dari bahasa Persia ghoul-e yabani atau ghoul-e biyabani, "raksasa liar" atau "raksasa padang") adalah binatang liar, makhluk luar biasa yang buas dan berbulu.
claims.quote: Qulyabanı (fars. غول یابانی‎ və ya غول بیابانی ğoul-e yabani və ya ğoul-e biyabani – "vəhşi nəhəng və ya düzənlik nəhəngi”) — Azərbaycan mifologiyasında vəhşi heyvan, fövqəladə, yırtıcı canlı, tüklü varlıq.

claims.statement: Hiiden hirvi ("Hiisi's moose") is a mythical moose of Finnish mythology that must be hunted on skis; the myth describes the creation of skis and the origin of the moose.
claims.statement_id: Hiiden hirvi ("rusa besar milik Hiisi") adalah rusa besar (moose) mitos dalam mitologi Finlandia yang harus diburu dengan bermain ski; mitos ini menceritakan penciptaan ski dan asal-usul rusa besar.
claims.quote: Hiiden hirvi (lit. 'Hiisi's moose') is a mythical moose in Finnish mythology which must be hunted by skiing. This myth describes the creation of skis and the origin of the moose.

claims.statement: The Estonian equivalent of Hiiden hirvi is Hiiehobune ("Hiis's horse").
claims.statement_id: Padanan Estonia dari Hiiden hirvi adalah Hiiehobune ("kuda milik Hiis").
claims.quote: The Estonian equivalent of Hiiden hirvi is Hiiehobune (lit. 'Hiis's horse').

claims.statement: In White Karelian and Olonets versions the hero reaches a place where women laugh, children cry and dogs bark, because Hiiden hirvi has just passed through and spoiled the food; the hero begins the chase, but one ski breaks and the moose escapes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Karelia Putih dan Olonets, sang tokoh tiba di tempat perempuan tertawa, anak-anak menangis, dan anjing menggonggong, karena Hiiden hirvi baru saja lewat dan merusak makanan; ia mulai memburu rusa itu, tetapi salah satu skinya patah dan rusa itu lolos.
claims.quote: The protagonist arrives at a location where women laugh, children cry and dogs bark. They tell the protagonist this is because Hiiden hirvi just passed through the area and ruined the food. The protagonist starts their chase of the moose but one of the skis break and the moose escapes.

claims.statement: In Ladoga Karelian versions the hero is usually "Lappalainen" (a Sámi person), sometimes named Lauri; in one version the hero is Väinämöinen, who succeeds in hunting the moose.
claims.statement_id: Dalam versi Karelia Ladoga, tokohnya biasanya "Lappalainen" (orang Sami), kadang bernama Lauri; dalam satu versi tokohnya Väinämöinen, yang berhasil memburu rusa itu.
claims.quote: In Ladoga Karelian versions, the protagonist is usually "Lappalainen" (a Sámi person). He might be given the name Lauri. In one version, the protagonist is Väinämöinen and in this case, he succeeds in hunting the moose.

claims.statement: Hiie põder (also hiie hirv; Finnish hiiden hirvi) is a supernatural animal of the Finnish epic Kalevala, described as hard to catch, swift and strong.
claims.statement_id: Hiie põder (juga hiie hirv; bahasa Finlandia hiiden hirvi) adalah hewan gaib dalam epos Finlandia Kalevala, yang digambarkan sulit ditangkap, cepat, dan kuat.
claims.quote: Hiie põder (ka hiie hirv; soome keeles hiiden hirvi) on üleloomulik loom soome eeposes "Kalevala". Seda looma on kirjeldatud kui raskesti püütavat, kiiret ja tugevat.

claims.statement: In the epic, Louhi sets her daughters' suitors the task of catching the hiie põder alive.
claims.statement_id: Dalam epos itu, Louhi memberi para pelamar putrinya tugas menangkap hiie põder hidup-hidup.
claims.quote: Eeposes annab Louhi oma tütarde kosilastele ülesandeks püüda hiie põder kinni elavana.

claims.statement: Kłobuk is the name of a kobold (house spirit) whose stories are told in southern Warmia (Olsztyn County in Poland's Warmian-Masurian Voivodeship); it is a spirit appearing as a feathered creature, a cat or a human.
claims.statement_id: Kłobuk adalah nama kobold (roh rumah) yang kisahnya diceritakan di Warmia selatan (Kabupaten Olsztyn, Provinsi Warmia-Masuria, Polandia); ia roh yang muncul sebagai makhluk berbulu unggas, kucing, atau manusia.
claims.quote: Kłobuk ist der Name eines Kobolds, dessen Geschichten im südlichen Ermland (Powiat Olsztyński in der polnischen Woiwodschaft Ermland-Masuren) erzählt werden. Es handelt sich um einen Geist, der in Gestalt eines gefiederten Wesens, einer Katze oder als Mensch auftritt.

claims.statement: Though described as a nuisance, it brings the household luck and prosperity, often by stealing from the owner's neighbours.
claims.statement_id: Meski digambarkan merepotkan, ia membawa keberuntungan dan kemakmuran bagi rumah tangga, sering dengan mencuri dari tetangga pemiliknya.
claims.quote: Obwohl er als lästig beschrieben wird, bringt er dem Haushalt Glück und Wohlstand, oftmals indem er die Nachbarn des Besitzers bestiehlt.

claims.statement: This enriching spirit was believed to be hatched from a special egg (of a black hen or a "cock's egg"), found by chance after heavy rain as a wet chick, or even bought from people "in the know".
claims.statement_id: Roh pembawa kekayaan ini dipercaya bisa ditetaskan dari telur khusus (telur ayam hitam atau "telur ayam jantan"), ditemukan secara kebetulan setelah hujan lebat dalam wujud anak ayam basah, atau bahkan dibeli dari orang yang "tahu".
claims.quote: Считалось, что духа-обогатителя можно вывести из особого яйца (чёрной курицы или из «петушиного»), либо просто найти случайно после сильного ливня в виде мокрого цыплёнка, птенца (либо даже купить у «знающих» людей)

claims.statement: Kłobuk or kołbuk is, in Slavic belief, a demon guarding property and the household hearth, identified with the soul of a dead foetus, most often taking the form of a drenched hen, but also a duck, goose, magpie, crow, cat or even a human.
claims.statement_id: Kłobuk atau kołbuk dalam kepercayaan Slavia adalah demon penjaga harta dan perapian rumah, disamakan dengan jiwa janin yang mati, dan paling sering berwujud ayam betina basah, juga bebek, angsa, murai, gagak, kucing, bahkan manusia.
claims.quote: Kłobuk, kołbuk – w wierzeniach słowiańskich demon opiekujący się dobytkiem i ogniskiem domowym. Utożsamiany z duszą martwego płodu. Przybierał najczęściej postać zmokłej kury, a także kaczki, gęsi, sroki, wrony, kota, a nawet człowieka.

claims.statement: Belief in kłobuks was alive mainly in the southern (Polish-speaking) areas of former East Prussia, above all among the Warmians of southern Warmia, less among the Masurians, and also in Silesia.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan pada kłobuk hidup terutama di wilayah selatan (berbahasa Polandia) bekas Prusia Timur, terutama di kalangan orang Warmia selatan, lebih sedikit di kalangan orang Masuria, serta di Silesia.
claims.quote: Wiara w kłobuki żywa była głównie w południowych (polskojęzycznych) rejonach dawnych Prus Wschodnich, przede wszystkim wśród Warmiaków (z południowej Warmii), w mniejszym zakresie wśród Mazurów, jak również na Śląsku.

claims.statement: The kłobuk increased its master's wealth, but by robbing the neighbours; it demanded care and a separate black-painted room at the end of the attic or another hard-to-reach place, and if badly treated it could take revenge.
claims.statement_id: Kłobuk melipatgandakan harta tuannya, tetapi dengan mencuri dari tetangga; ia menuntut perawatan dan kamar khusus bercat hitam di ujung loteng atau tempat sulit dijangkau, dan bila diperlakukan buruk ia bisa membalas dendam.
claims.quote: Kłobuk dbał o pomnożenie majątku swojego gospodarza. Czynił to jednak, okradając sąsiadów. Od swojego właściciela wymagał opieki, a także osobnego, pomalowanego na czarno pokoju, znajdującego się na końcu strychu lub w innym, trudno dostępnym miejscu. Źle potraktowany, może się mścić.

claims.statement: Kanjirottu Yakshi is a folk deity of South India; by the myth she was born into the Mangalathu family at Kanjiracode in Southern Travancore (now Tamil Nadu), also called Chiruthevi, a beautiful courtesan; she became a yakshi after being murdered by her palanquin-bearer, waylaying men with her beauty and drinking their blood.
claims.statement_id: Kanjirottu Yakshi adalah dewi rakyat India Selatan; menurut mitos ia lahir dalam keluarga Mangalathu di Kanjiracode, Travancore Selatan (kini Tamil Nadu), dikenal juga sebagai Chiruthevi, seorang pelacur istana jelita; ia menjadi yakshi setelah dibunuh pemikul tandunya, lalu memikat lelaki dengan kecantikannya dan meminum darah mereka.
claims.quote: Kanjirottu Yakshi is a folkloric deity of South India. According to the myth, she was born into the Mangalathu family at Kanjiracode in Southern Travancore (now in Tamil Nadu). Also known as Chiruthevi, she was a beautiful courtesan ... She turned into a Yakshi after being murdered by her palanquin-bearer, waylaying men with her beauty and drinking their blood.

claims.statement: She fell in love with Kunjuraman, her palanquin-bearer, who carried her and her brother Govindan, but Kunjuraman was already married and did not return her feelings.
claims.statement_id: Ia jatuh cinta kepada Kunjuraman, pemikul tandunya yang biasa memikul dia dan saudaranya Govindan, tetapi Kunjuraman sudah menikah dan tidak membalas perasaannya.
claims.quote: However, she fell in love with Kunjuraman, her palanquin-bearer, who would carry both her and her brother Govindan around on his back. However, Kunjuraman was already married and did not reciprocate Chiruthevi's feelings.

claims.statement: Frustrated, Chiruthevi had Kunjuraman's wife killed; when Govindan found out and told Kunjuraman, Kunjuraman agreed to sleep with Chiruthevi and strangled her in bed to avenge his wife.
claims.statement_id: Kecewa, Chiruthevi mengatur pembunuhan istri Kunjuraman; ketika Govindan mengetahuinya dan memberi tahu Kunjuraman, Kunjuraman bersedia tidur dengan Chiruthevi lalu mencekiknya di ranjang untuk membalas kematian istrinya.
claims.quote: Frustrated by Kunjuraman's romantic indifference towards her, Chiruthevi arranged for Kunjuraman's wife to be killed. When Govindan found out that his sister was behind the plot, he told Kunjuraman, who agreed to sleep with Chiruthevi. While they were in bed, Kunjuraman strangled Chiruthevi in order to avenge the murder of his wife.

claims.statement: After her murder Chiruthevi was reborn as a yakshi to a couple in Kanjirottu and moments after birth magically became a bewitching woman; as a yakshi she seduced and terrorised men and drank their blood, never ceasing to harass Kunjuraman, whom she still desired.
claims.statement_id: Setelah dibunuh, Chiruthevi lahir kembali sebagai yakshi dari pasangan di Kanjirottu dan sesaat setelah lahir berubah secara gaib menjadi perempuan yang memikat; sebagai yakshi ia menggoda dan meneror lelaki serta meminum darah mereka, dan terus mengganggu Kunjuraman yang masih ia inginkan.
claims.quote: Following her murder, Chiruthevi was reborn as a yakshi to a couple in Kanjirottu. She magically transformed into a bewitchingly beautiful woman moments after her birth. As a yakshi, she proceeded to seduce and terrorize men and drink their blood, never forgetting to harass the still-living Kunjuraman, whom she still desired.

claims.statement: Folklore says she took refuge in the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple; today she is worshipped in a small shrine (Thekkedom) within the temple complex as a protector deity who traded her thirst for blood for spiritual devotion.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat, ia berlindung di Kuil Sree Padmanabhaswamy, dan kini dipuja di sebuah tempat suci kecil (Thekkedom) di kompleks kuil itu sebagai dewi pelindung yang telah menukar haus darahnya dengan pengabdian spiritual.
claims.quote: Folklore states that, she sought refuge in the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple. Today, she is worshipped in a small shrine (Thekkedom) within the temple complex, where she is seen as a protector deity who has traded her thirst for blood for spiritual devotion.

claims.statement: The lidérc is a unique supernatural being of Hungarian folklore with three varieties that often borrow traits from one another; the first, more traditional form is a miracle chicken (csodacsirke) hatched from a black hen's first egg kept warm under a person's arm.
claims.statement_id: Lidérc adalah makhluk gaib khas cerita rakyat Hungaria dengan tiga ragam yang sering saling meminjam ciri; bentuk pertama yang lebih tradisional adalah anak ayam ajaib (csodacsirke) yang menetas dari telur pertama ayam hitam yang dihangatkan di bawah ketiak manusia.
claims.quote: is a unique supernatural being of Hungarian folklore. It has three known varieties, which often borrow traits from one another. The first, more traditional form of the lidérc is as a miracle chicken, csodacsirke in Hungarian, which hatches from the first egg of a black hen kept warm under the arm of a human.

claims.statement: The lidérc attaches itself to people as their lover; fondling its victim, sitting on her body and sometimes sucking her blood until she grows weak and ill; hence the Hungarian word for nightmare, lidércnyomás, "lidérc pressure".
claims.statement_id: Lidérc melekat pada manusia untuk menjadi kekasihnya; ia menggerayangi korbannya, duduk di tubuhnya, kadang mengisap darahnya hingga perempuan itu lemah dan sakit; dari sinilah kata Hungaria untuk mimpi buruk, lidércnyomás, "tekanan lidérc".
claims.quote: The lidérc attaches itself to people to become their lover. ... it fondles her, sits on her body, and sometimes sucks her blood, making her weak and sick after a time. From this source comes a Hungarian word for nightmare -- lidércnyomás, which literally means "lidérc pressure", from the pressure on the body while the being sits on it.

claims.statement: The lidérc hoards gold and so makes its owner rich; to get rid of it, it must be persuaded to do an impossible task, such as hauling sand with a rope or water with a sieve, or it can be destroyed by locking it in a tree hollow.
claims.statement_id: Lidérc menimbun emas sehingga pemiliknya kaya; untuk menyingkirkannya, ia harus dibujuk mengerjakan tugas mustahil, seperti mengangkut pasir dengan tali atau air dengan saringan, atau dimusnahkan dengan dikurung dalam lubang pohon.
claims.quote: The lidérc hoards gold and thus makes its owner rich. To dispose of this form of the lidérc, it must be persuaded to perform an impossible task, such as haul sand with rope, or water with a sieve. It can also be destroyed by locking it into a tree hollow.

claims.statement: The third variety is the satanic lover (ördögszerető), much like an incubus or succubus, which flies at night as a fiery light, a will-o'-the-wisp or a bird of fire.
claims.statement_id: Ragam ketiga adalah kekasih setan (ördögszerető), mirip incubus atau succubus, yang terbang pada malam hari sebagai cahaya berapi, api tipuan, atau burung api.
claims.quote: The third variety is as a Satanic lover, ördögszerető in Hungarian, quite similar to an incubus or succubus. This form of the lidérc flies at night, appearing as a fiery light, a will o' the wisp, or even as a bird of fire.

claims.statement: The lidérc (also lüdérc, lúdvérc, lederc, lidroc, lidröc, inglice and so on) is a demon of Hungarian mythology widespread in folk tradition.
claims.statement_id: Lidérc (juga lüdérc, lúdvérc, lederc, lidroc, lidröc, inglice, dan lain-lain) adalah demon mitologi Hungaria yang tersebar luas dalam tradisi rakyat.
claims.quote: A lidérc (lüdérc, lúdvérc, lederc, lidroc, lidröc, inglice stb) a magyar mitológia démona, mely a néphagyományban szélesen elterjedt.

claims.statement: The names may differ, but every people's folklore agrees that, however useful it may be, because of its evil nature it must be got rid of as soon as possible.
claims.statement_id: Namanya bisa berbeda-beda, tetapi folklor semua bangsa sepakat bahwa betapapun bergunanya, karena sifatnya yang jahat ia harus disingkirkan secepat mungkin.
claims.quote: Az elnevezések különbözőek lehetnek, de minden nép folklórja megegyezik abban, bármilyen hasznos is lehet, gonosz természete miatt minél hamarabb meg kell szabadulni tőle.

claims.statement: In Estonian folk religion, maa-alused are mysterious elf-like creatures that live beneath the ground.
claims.statement_id: Dalam agama rakyat Estonia, maa-alused adalah makhluk misterius mirip peri yang hidup di bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Maa-alused are, in Estonian folk religion, mysterious elf-like creatures which live beneath the ground.

claims.statement: They were believed to live a parallel existence to humans, the main differences being that all orientations are reversed, up becoming down and left becoming right, and that everything they own is smaller in size.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dipercaya hidup sejajar dengan manusia, dengan perbedaan utama bahwa semua arah terbalik, atas menjadi bawah dan kiri menjadi kanan, dan semua milik mereka berukuran lebih kecil.
claims.quote: They were believed to have a parallel existence to that of humans, the principal differences being that all orientations are reversed, such that up becomes down and left becomes right, and that all things possessed by them are diminished in size.

claims.statement: The Portuguese article likewise calls maa-alused mysterious elfin creatures of Estonian mythology living under the earth.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Portugis juga menyebut maa-alused sebagai makhluk misterius mirip peri dalam mitologia Estonia yang hidup di bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Maa-alused eram, na mitologia estoniana, misteriosas criaturas élficas, as quais viviam sob a terra.

claims.statement: Maa-alused (also maahaldjad) were originally dead beings who later lived under the ground or under the floor.
claims.statement_id: Maa-alused (juga disebut maahaldjad) semula adalah makhluk yang sudah mati, yang kemudian hidup di bawah tanah atau di bawah lantai.
claims.quote: Maa-alused (ka maahaldjad) olid algselt surnud olendid, kes hiljem elasid maa või põranda all.

claims.statement: Maa-alused were known as tiny human-shaped mythical beings mainly in North Estonia (Põhja-Eesti), whose presence was signalled by sounds; they worked as smiths (hammering tiks-tiks) and weavers, appeared above ground as insects or animals (usually frogs), and repaid good deeds generously.
claims.statement_id: Maa-alused dikenal sebagai makhluk mitos kecil berwujud manusia, terutama di Estonia Utara (Põhja-Eesti), yang keberadaannya ditandai suara-suara; mereka bekerja sebagai pandai besi (berbunyi tiks-tiks) dan penenun, muncul di atas tanah sebagai serangga atau hewan (biasanya katak), dan membalas kebaikan dengan murah hati.
claims.quote: Maa-alused olid tuntud pisikeste inimesekujuliste mütoloogiliste olenditena põhiliselt Põhja-Eestis, nende olemasolust andsid märku hääled. Nad tegutsesid seppade (taovad tiks-tiks) ja kangrutena, maa peale ilmusid ka putuka või loomana (harilikult konnana). Neile tehtud heategude eest tasusid rikkalikult.

claims.statement: Angering the maa-alused and maahaldjad (found in South Estonian, Lõuna-Eesti, folk tradition) could bring a disease from the earth, itself also called maa-alused; mainly on Saaremaa, people were not allowed to step on insects or their paths so as not to anger the maa-alused.
claims.statement_id: Membuat marah maa-alused dan maahaldjad (yang muncul dalam tradisi rakyat Estonia Selatan, Lõuna-Eesti) bisa mendatangkan penyakit dari tanah, yang juga disebut maa-alused; terutama di Saaremaa, orang tidak boleh menginjak serangga atau jalur mereka agar maa-alused tidak marah.
claims.quote: Maa-aluste ja maahaldjate (kes esinesid Lõuna-Eesti rahvapärimustes) pahandamine võis kaasa tuua maast saadud haiguse (haigust nimetati samuti maa-alused). Peamiselt Saaremaal ei olnud lubatud putukate peale või nende teeradadele astumine, et mitte pahandada maa-aluseid.

claims.statement: Marțolea is a demonic entity of Romanian mythology, especially in Bucovina and Maramureș; its gender is unclear since it can shapeshift at will, and it lives in the mountains and comes down on Tuesday nights to lure with its singing and punish women caught working.
claims.statement_id: Marțolea adalah entitas demonik dalam mitologi Rumania, terutama di Bucovina dan Maramureș; jenis kelaminnya tidak jelas karena ia bisa berubah wujud sesuka hati, ia tinggal di pegunungan dan turun pada malam Selasa untuk memikat dengan nyanyiannya dan menghukum perempuan yang kedapatan bekerja.
claims.quote: Marțolea is a demonic entity in Romanian mythology (especially in the regions of Bucovina and Maramureș). The entity's gender is unclear, as it can shapeshift at will. It lives up in the mountains and descends on Tuesday nights to lure with its singing and punish the women caught working.

claims.statement: Also called Marț-sara or Marți Seara (old Romanian for "Tuesday Evening"), it is a malefic entity that demands the semi-holy day of Tuesday be respected and forbids four women's chores: spinning wool, sowing, boiling laundry and baking bread.
claims.statement_id: Dikenal juga sebagai Marț-sara atau Marți Seara ("Selasa Malam" dalam bahasa Rumania lama), ia entitas jahat yang menuntut hari Selasa yang setengah suci dihormati dan melarang empat pekerjaan perempuan: memintal wol, menjahit, merebus cucian, dan memanggang roti.
claims.quote: Also known as Marț-sara or Marți Seara (the old Romanian words for "Tuesday Evening"), it is a malefic entity who demands the semi-holy day of Tuesday to be respected and who forbids four women's chores: spinning of the wool, sowing, boiling laundry and baking bread.

claims.statement: Usually it has the form of a goat with a human-like head, horns and hooves; it can become an ugly old woman all in white, a soldier or a handsome man; to married women it appears as an old woman, to married men as a virgin, and to unmarried women as a charming young man.
claims.statement_id: Biasanya ia berwujud kambing berkepala mirip manusia, bertanduk dan berkuku belah; ia bisa menjadi perempuan tua buruk rupa berpakaian serba putih, prajurit, atau lelaki tampan; kepada perempuan bersuami ia tampil sebagai perempuan tua, kepada lelaki beristri sebagai perawan, dan kepada perempuan lajang sebagai pemuda memikat.
claims.quote: Usually its form is of a goat with a human-like head, horns and hooves. It can shapeshift into an ugly, old woman dressed all in white, a soldier or as a handsome man. To married women, it shows as an old woman; to married men as a virgin, and to unmarried women as a young charming man.

claims.statement: According to Simeon Florea Marian (1847–1907) in Mitologie românească, Marțolea is a mythological figure spread across the whole Romanian territory.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Simeon Florea Marian (1847–1907) dalam Mitologie românească, Marțolea adalah tokoh mitologi yang tersebar di seluruh wilayah Rumania.
claims.quote: Marțolea este un personaj mitologic, răspândit pe întreg teritoriul românesc, după cum precizează Simeon Florea Marian (1847-1907), în Mitologie românească

claims.statement: Marțolea patronises Tuesday (marți) evenings, hence also the name Marțsara, and is also patron of 1 March (Martie), that is of the Mărțișor; glad to see girls wearing it, it gives a mart or mărțișor, a coin of pure silver worn at the neck all year.
claims.statement_id: Marțolea menaungi malam-malam Selasa (marți), sehingga disebut juga Marțsara, dan juga pelindung tanggal 1 Maret (Martie), yakni Mărțișor; senang melihat gadis-gadis memakainya, ia menghadiahkan mart atau mărțișor, yaitu koin perak murni yang dikalungkan sepanjang tahun.
claims.quote: Marțolea patronează serile de marți, din care cauză se mai numește și Marțsara, dar este și patronul zilei de 1 Martie, respectiv al Mărțișorului. ... Fericit că fetele îl poartă, el dăruiește un mart sau un mărțișor, adică un ban de argint curat, care se poartă la gât tot anul.

claims.statement: Marțolea's punishment was downright sadistic: it threw a host of spindles down the chimney to the guilty women, who had to fill them with spun wool, weave cloth from the thread and make it a garment by dawn; whoever failed died.
claims.statement_id: Hukuman dari Marțolea sungguh kejam: ia melemparkan banyak sekali gelendong lewat cerobong kepada perempuan yang bersalah, yang harus mereka isi dengan benang wol; dari benang itu mereka harus menenun kain dan menjahit pakaian untuknya sebelum fajar, dan yang gagal akan mati.
claims.quote: Pedeapsa administrată de Marțolea era de-a dreptul sadică: le arunca împricinatelor pe horn o puzderie de fuse, pe care bietele femei trebuiau să le umple cu lână toarsă. Din firul care rezulta trebuiau să îi țeasă o pânză și să-i facă din ea o haină până în zori. Cine nu reușea, murea.

claims.statement: In Doina Ruști's Dicționar de teme și simboluri, Marțolea also appears as a malefic lover who eats the hearts of the girls it falls for, and its animal forms bring it close to Silenus, Pan and Mars (Silen, Pan, Marte).
claims.statement_id: Dalam Dicționar de teme și simboluri karya Doina Ruști, Marțolea juga tampil sebagai kekasih jahat yang memakan jantung gadis yang ia cintai, dan wujud hewannya mendekatkannya pada Silenus, Pan, dan Mars (Silen, Pan, Marte).
claims.quote: În Dicționar de teme și simboluri de Doina Ruști, Marțolea apare și ca îndrăgostit malefic, care mănâncă inima fetelor de care se îndrăgostește. Zoomorfismele sale îl apropie de Silen, de Pan și de Marte.

claims.statement: Marțolea repays women who keep Tuesday holy by leaving eggs on their doorstep or flowers from the highest mountains of Bukovina.
claims.statement_id: Marțolea membalas perempuan yang menyucikan hari Selasa dengan meninggalkan telur di ambang pintu atau bunga dari pegunungan tertinggi di Bukovina.
claims.quote: Marțolea repays the women who keep the Tuesday day sacred by leaving them eggs on their doorstep or flowers from the highest mountains in Bukovina.

claims.statement: The Ora (Albanian orë, definite form ora) is an Albanian mythological figure that every human has from birth, tied to destiny and fate; its essential function is to maintain the order of the universe and enforce its laws.
claims.statement_id: Ora (bahasa Albania orë, bentuk takrif ora) adalah tokoh mitologi Albania yang dimiliki setiap manusia sejak lahir, terkait nasib dan takdir; fungsi utamanya menjaga tatanan alam semesta dan menegakkan hukumnya.
claims.quote: The Ora (Albanian: orë, definite form: ora, pl.: orë/t) is an Albanian mythological figure that every human possesses from birth, associated with human destiny and fate. The essential function of the ora is to maintain the order of the universe and to enforce its laws.

claims.statement: In Albanian folklore and poetry the Ora is a protective spirit everyone has from birth, and its appearance changes with the person's character: a white Ora for the brave and industrious, a black Ora for the lazy or cowardly.
claims.statement_id: Dalam folklor dan puisi Albania, Ora adalah roh pelindung yang dimiliki setiap manusia sejak lahir, dan rupanya berubah menurut watak orangnya: Ora putih bagi yang berani dan rajin, Ora hitam bagi yang malas atau pengecut.
claims.quote: Within Albanian folklore and poetry, the Ora is a protective spirit that every human possesses from birth. The Ora's appearance alters according to the personality and attributes of the human – “a white Ora for the brave and industrious, or a black Ora for the lazy or cowardly.”

claims.statement: The Ora dwell north of the Drin River in Northern Albania; in Central Albania they were believed to be everywhere, listening to people's blessings and curses and trying to fulfil them quickly, while outside Central Albania they live in forests and mountains, in streams, lakes and caves.
claims.statement_id: Ora berdiam di utara Sungai Drin di Albania Utara; di Albania Tengah mereka dipercaya hadir di mana-mana, mendengarkan berkat dan kutuk orang lalu berusaha cepat mewujudkannya, sedangkan di luar Albania Tengah mereka tinggal di hutan dan gunung, di sungai kecil, danau, dan gua.
claims.quote: The Ora reside towards the north of the Drin River in Northern Albania. Within Central Albania it was believed that the Ora were present everywhere, “listening to people’s blessings and curses, which they would then aim to quickly fulfil”. Outside of Central Albania Oras live in forests and mountains, residing in streams, lakes, and caves.

claims.statement: The Ora could take any form, including birds, beasts, women or serpents; in Northern Albania they often appear as serpents, like the Southern Albanian deity Vitore, and both are depicted as a golden-horned serpent that brings gold.
claims.statement_id: Ora bisa mengambil wujud apa pun, termasuk burung, binatang buas, perempuan, atau ular; di Albania Utara mereka sering muncul sebagai ular, seperti dewi Vitore di Albania Selatan, dan keduanya digambarkan sebagai ular bertanduk emas yang membawa emas.
claims.quote: Within Albanian folklore and poetry, Ora had the ability to take any form they pleased, including “birds, beasts, women, or serpents.” ... In Northern Albania, Oras “often appear as serpents.” – similarly to the Southern Albanian deity Vitore. Both the Ora and Vitore are “widely represented as a serpent with golden horns who brings gold.”

claims.statement: In Northern Albania the Oras are represented, like the Southern Albanian Fatia, as a group of three goddesses who gather at night to determine a child's fate at birth and bestow their favours on it.
claims.statement_id: Di Albania Utara, Ora digambarkan, seperti Fatia di Albania Selatan, sebagai kelompok tiga dewi yang berkumpul pada malam hari untuk menentukan nasib anak saat lahir dan membagikan anugerah mereka kepadanya.
claims.quote: In Northern Albania, the Oras are represented – similarly to the Southern Albanian Fatia – as a group of three mythological goddesses who gather in the night to perform the task of “determining the child’s fate at birth” and distribute their favours upon the child.

claims.statement: The Albanian article calls it Ora e maleve ("Ora of the mountains"), an Albanian mythological figure every person has from birth, tied to human fate and destiny.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Albania menyebutnya Ora e maleve ("Ora pegunungan"), tokoh mitologi Albania yang dimiliki setiap orang sejak lahir dan terkait nasib serta takdir manusia.
claims.quote: Ora e maleve (e pashquar: orë, e shquar: ora, shumës: orë/t) është një figurë mitologjike shqiptare që çdo njeri posedon që nga lindja, e lidhur me fatet dhe destinimin e njeriut.

claims.statement: The blinded Zuku, wandering aimlessly in the mountains, meets an ora who restores his sight with herbs and tells him to take vengeance.
claims.statement_id: Zuku yang dibutakan dan mengembara tanpa arah di pegunungan bertemu ora yang memulihkan penglihatannya dengan ramuan dan menyuruhnya membalas dendam.
claims.quote: Wandering aimlessly in the mountains, the blind Zuku is met by an ora who restores his sights with some herbs and tells him to take vengeance

claims.statement: Paha (Finnish, "evil", Übel) is a demonic spirit of Finnish mythology and a follower of Lempo, the god of malice.
claims.statement_id: Paha (bahasa Finlandia, "kejahatan", Übel) adalah roh demonik dalam mitologi Finlandia dan pengikut Lempo, dewa kejahatan.
claims.quote: Paha (finnisch; deutsch: Übel) ist ein Dämonischer Geist aus der finnischen Mythologie. Er ist ein Anhänger von Lempo, dem Gott der Bosheit.

claims.statement: When Väinämöinen fought the demons, Paha together with Hiisi made Väinämöinen wound himself with his own axe.
claims.statement_id: Ketika Väinämöinen bertarung melawan para demon, Paha bersama Hiisi membuat Väinämöinen melukai dirinya sendiri dengan kapaknya.
claims.quote: Als Väinämöinen gegen die Dämonen kämpfte, sorgte Paha zusammen mit Hiisi dafür, dass Väinämöinen sich mit seiner eigenen Axt selbst verletzte.

claims.statement: The Catalan article also calls Paha (Catalan dolent, "bad") a demonic spirit of Finnish mythology and a follower of Lempo, the god of malice.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Katalan juga menyebut Paha (bahasa Katalan dolent, "jahat") sebagai roh demonik mitologi Finlandia dan pengikut Lempo, dewa kedengkian.
claims.quote: Paha (del finès; en català: dolent) és un esperit demoníac de la mitologia finesa. És un seguidor de Lempo, el déu de la malícia.

claims.statement: The Japanese article describes Paha as an evil spirit appearing in Finnish mythology.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Jepang menyebut Paha sebagai roh jahat yang muncul dalam mitologi Finlandia.
claims.quote: パハ（フィンランド語: Paha）は、フィンランド神話に登場する悪霊。

claims.statement: In the Kalevala, Paha appears in the scene where Väinämöinen hews wood with an axe to build a boat to win the Maiden of Pohjola (chapter 8, around lines 151–154), and together with the evil spirits Hiisi and Lempo wounds Väinämöinen.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Kalevala, Paha muncul pada adegan Väinämöinen memahat kayu dengan kapak untuk membuat perahu demi mendapatkan gadis Pohjola (bab 8, sekitar baris 151–154), dan bersama roh jahat Hiisi dan Lempo melukai Väinämöinen.
claims.quote: 『カレワラ』では、ワイナミョイネンがポホヨラの乙女（フィンランド語版）を手に入れるため斧で木を削って船を造っている場面（第8章151-154行目前後）で登場し、同じく悪霊のヒーシ（英語版）、レンポ（英語版） とともにワイナミョイネンに傷を負わせている。

claims.statement: The quoted Kalevala lines run: on the third day Hiisi twisted the axe-butt, Lempo snatched the blade, Paha shook the handle (Niin päivällä kolmannella Hiisi pontta pyörähytti, Lempo tempasi tereä, Paha vartta vaapahutti).
claims.statement_id: Baris Kalevala yang dikutip berbunyi: pada hari ketiga Hiisi memutar ujung kapak, Lempo merenggut matanya, Paha menggoyang gagangnya.
claims.quote: Niin päivällä kolmannella Hiisi pontta pyörähytti, Lempo tempasi tereä, Paha vartta vaapahutti.

claims.statement: Through the mischief of Paha and the others, the axe struck a stone, glanced off and wounded Väinämöinen's knee; the blood flowed without stopping and Väinämöinen had to struggle to staunch it (chapters 8–9).
claims.statement_id: Karena ulah Paha dan kawan-kawannya, kapak itu membentur batu, terpental, dan melukai lutut Väinämöinen; darah mengalir tanpa henti dan Väinämöinen harus berusaha keras menghentikannya (bab 8–9).
claims.quote: パハたちの悪さにより、斧が石に当たり跳ね返り、ワイナミョイネンの膝に当たって傷を負わせた。傷からは血が流れだし止まることがなく、血を止めるためワイナミョイネンは奔走することになる（第8-9章）。

claims.statement: The asteroid Paha is named after this figure, and together with Lempo and Hiisi it forms a triple asteroid system.
claims.statement_id: Nama asteroid Paha berasal dari tokoh ini, dan bersama Lempo dan Hiisi asteroid itu membentuk sistem asteroid rangkap tiga.
claims.quote: 小惑星パハの名前はこのパハに由来する。レンポ、ヒーシとともに三重小惑星を成している。

claims.statement: Rahko or Rahkoi is a figure of Finnish mythology first mentioned in writing in 1551 by Mikael Agricola as one who "split the Moon black" ("Rachkoi Cuun mustaxi jacoi"), so he has been linked to the waning of the Moon.
claims.statement_id: Rahko atau Rahkoi adalah tokoh mitologi Finlandia yang pertama kali disebut secara tertulis pada 1551 oleh Mikael Agricola sebagai sosok yang "membelah Bulan menjadi hitam" ("Rachkoi Cuun mustaxi jacoi"), sehingga ia dikaitkan dengan memudarnya Bulan.
claims.quote: Rahko or Rahkoi is a figure in Finnish mythology. He was first mentioned in writing in 1551 by Mikael Agricola as someone who "split the Moon black" ("Rachkoi Cuun mustaxi jacoi"), so he has been connected to the waning of the Moon.

claims.statement: In 1789 Christfried Ganander wrote that Rahkoi is a ghost the Tavastians of old believed blackened the Moon.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1789 Christfried Ganander menulis bahwa Rahkoi adalah hantu yang menurut kepercayaan orang Tavastia zaman dulu menghitamkan Bulan.
claims.quote: In 1789, Christfried Ganander wrote that Rahkoi is a ghost who the Tavastians of old believed blackened the Moon.

claims.statement: In South Ostrobothnia, Rahko has meant a nightmare.
claims.statement_id: Di Ostrobothnia Selatan, kata Rahko berarti mimpi buruk.
claims.quote: In South Ostrobothnia, Rahko has meant a nightmare.

claims.statement: In Forest Finnish beliefs, the kapeet ate the moon away every month and Rahko, someone who had committed suicide, forged a new moon from cow's hooves and fat; after being Rahko long enough one became a kave and a new Rahko took one's place.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan orang Finlandia Hutan, para kapeet memakan bulan setiap bulan dan Rahko, seseorang yang mati bunuh diri, menempa bulan baru dari kuku dan lemak sapi; setelah cukup lama menjadi Rahko, ia menjadi kave dan Rahko baru menggantikannya.
claims.quote: In Forest Finnish beliefs, kapeet ate the moon away every month and Rahko, someone who had committed suicide, forged a new moon from cow's hooves and fat. After being a Rahko for long enough, you'd become a kave, and a new Rahko took your place.

claims.statement: The Sámi in Finland knew Mano-Rakko ("Rakko of the Moon"), a thief who went up to the Moon to cover it in tar so its light would not give him away; but he got stuck and can still be seen on the Moon with a tar bucket in one hand and a brush in the other.
claims.statement_id: Orang Sami di Finlandia mengenal Mano-Rakko ("Rakko dari Bulan"), pencuri yang naik ke Bulan untuk melumurinya dengan ter agar cahayanya tidak membongkar dirinya; tetapi ia tersangkut dan masih terlihat di Bulan, memegang ember ter dan kuas.
claims.quote: The Sámi in Finland knew a figure called Mano-Rakko ("Rakko of the Moon"), who had been a thief who had gone up to the Moon to cover it in tar so its light wouldn't give him away. However, he got stuck and can still be seen on the Moon, a bucket of tar in one hand and a brush in the other.

claims.statement: The Italian article says Rahko, also known as Raako, is regarded in Finnish and Karelian (careliana) mythology as a deity of time and of the waning phases of the moon.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Italia menyebut Rahko, juga dikenal sebagai Raako, dalam mitologi Finlandia dan Karelia (careliana) sebagai dewa waktu dan memudarnya fase bulan.
claims.quote: Rahko conosciuto anche come Raako nella mitologia finlandese ed in quella careliana è considerato una divinità del tempo e del declino delle fasi della luna

claims.statement: Rahko also appears as the name of a disease and as an evil household spirit (kodinhaltija).
claims.statement_id: Rahko juga muncul sebagai nama penyakit dan sebagai roh rumah (kodinhaltija) yang jahat.
claims.quote: Rahko esiintyy myös taudin nimenä ja pahana kodinhaltijana.

claims.statement: Kaarle Krohn believed the word rahko means "chapping"; the Veps have a similar being appearing as a drying-barn haltija (rihenrahkoi) or an oven haltija (päčinrahkoi).
claims.statement_id: Kaarle Krohn berpendapat kata rahko berarti "kulit pecah-pecah"; orang Veps punya makhluk serupa yang muncul sebagai haltija lumbung pengering (rihenrahkoi) atau haltija tungku (päčinrahkoi).
claims.quote: Kaarle Krohn believed the word rahko means "chapping". The Veps people have a similar being who appears as a riihi haltija (rihenrahkoi) or an oven haltija (päčinrahkoi).

claims.statement: The Richmond Vampire (locally also called the Hollywood Vampire) is an urban legend from Richmond, Virginia.
claims.statement_id: Vampir Richmond (secara lokal juga disebut Vampir Hollywood) adalah legenda urban dari Richmond, Virginia.
claims.quote: The Richmond Vampire (also called locally the Hollywood Vampire) is an urban legend from Richmond, Virginia.

claims.statement: Local residents claim that the mausoleum of W. W. Pool (dated 1913) in Hollywood Cemetery holds a vampire's remains; supposedly Pool was driven out of England in the 19th century for being a vampire, and oral legends to this effect circulated by the 1960s.
claims.statement_id: Warga setempat mengklaim bahwa mausoleum W. W. Pool (bertarikh 1913) di Pemakaman Hollywood menyimpan jasad vampir; konon Pool diusir dari Inggris pada abad ke-19 karena vampir, dan legenda lisan semacam ini sudah beredar pada 1960-an.
claims.quote: Local residents claim that the mausoleum of W. W. Pool (Dated 1913) in Hollywood Cemetery holds the remains of a vampire. Supposedly Pool was run out of England in the 19th century for being a vampire. Oral legends to this effect were circulating by the 1960s.

claims.statement: The legends may be influenced by the tomb's architecture, with Masonic and ancient Egyptian elements and double Ws resembling fangs; because the cemetery adjoins Virginia Commonwealth University, the story became popular among students especially from the 1980s, and it first appeared in print in the student newspaper Commonwealth Times in 1976.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini mungkin dipengaruhi arsitektur makam yang memiliki unsur Mason dan Mesir kuno serta dua huruf W yang mirip taring; karena pemakaman itu bersebelahan dengan Virginia Commonwealth University, ceritanya populer di kalangan mahasiswa terutama sejak 1980-an, dan pertama kali dicetak di koran mahasiswa Commonwealth Times pada 1976.
claims.quote: They may be influenced by the architecture of the tomb, which has both Masonic and ancient Egyptian elements, and double Ws looking like fangs. Because this cemetery is adjacent to Virginia Commonwealth University, the story became popular among students, especially from the 1980s onward. It was first mentioned in print in the student newspaper Commonwealth Times in 1976.

claims.statement: In this newer version, the tunnelling awakened an ancient evil living under Church Hill that brought the tunnel down on the workers; rescuers found an unearthly blood-covered creature with jagged teeth and skin hanging from its muscular body crouching over a victim.
claims.statement_id: Menurut versi yang lebih baru, penggalian terowongan membangunkan kejahatan purba yang hidup di bawah Church Hill dan meruntuhkan terowongan itu menimpa para pekerja; tim penyelamat menemukan makhluk berlumur darah bergigi bergerigi dengan kulit bergelantungan dari tubuh berotot, berjongkok di atas salah satu korban.
claims.quote: According to this newer story, the tunneling awakened an ancient evil that lived under Church Hill and brought the tunnel crashing down on the workers. Rescue teams found an unearthly blood-covered creature with jagged teeth and skin hanging from its muscular body crouching over one of the victims.

claims.statement: Since 2001 the vampire story has been combined with the collapse of the Chesapeake and Ohio Railroad's Church Hill Tunnel under Church Hill in eastern Richmond, which buried several workers on Friday, October 2, 1925; this part appeared online only in 2001 and in print first in 2007.
claims.statement_id: Sejak 2001, cerita vampir ini digabungkan dengan runtuhnya Terowongan Church Hill milik Chesapeake and Ohio Railroad di bawah Church Hill, Richmond timur, yang mengubur beberapa pekerja pada Jumat, 2 Oktober 1925; bagian cerita ini baru muncul daring pada 2001 dan pertama dicetak pada 2007.
claims.quote: Since 2001, the vampire story has been combined with the collapse of the Chesapeake and Ohio Railroad's Church Hill Tunnel under Church Hill, a neighborhood of eastern Richmond, Virginia, which buried several workers on Friday, October 2, 1925. This part of the story did not show up online until 2001 and was first reported in print in 2007

claims.statement: The Spanish article describes the Richmond Vampire as an urban legend of the city of Richmond, capital of the state of Virginia, United States (Estados Unidos).
claims.statement_id: Artikel Spanyol menyebut Vampir Richmond sebagai legenda urban dari kota Richmond, ibu kota negara bagian Virginia, Amerika Serikat (Estados Unidos).
claims.quote: El vampiro de Richmond hace referencia a una leyenda urbana de la ciudad homónima, capital del estado de Virginia (Estados Unidos).

claims.statement: In this explanation the "creature" that escaped the collapse was actually the 28-year-old railroad fireman Benjamin F. Mosby (1896–1925), who had been shovelling coal into a steam locomotive's firebox shirtless when the cave-in occurred and the boiler burst.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penjelasan ini, "makhluk" yang lolos dari runtuhnya terowongan sebenarnya adalah juru api kereta berusia 28 tahun, Benjamin F. Mosby (1896–1925), yang sedang menyekop batu bara ke tungku lokomotif uap tanpa baju ketika runtuhan terjadi dan ketelnya pecah.
claims.quote: the "creature" that escaped the tunnel collapse was actually the 28-year-old railroad fireman, Benjamin F. Mosby (1896-1925), who had been shoveling coal into the firebox of a steam locomotive of a work train with no shirt on when the cave-in occurred and the boiler ruptured.

claims.statement: Contemporary written records include none of these alleged details.
claims.statement_id: Catatan tertulis sezaman tidak memuat satu pun dari detail-detail yang diklaim itu.
claims.quote: Contemporary written records do not include any of these alleged details.

claims.statement: Rokita is a demon of Polish folklore said to inhabit gateways to the underworld, including wetlands, forests and the insides of old willow trees; in some local tales he is seen as an equivalent of Leshy.
claims.statement_id: Rokita adalah demon dalam cerita rakyat Polandia yang konon mendiami gerbang ke dunia bawah, termasuk lahan basah, hutan, dan bagian dalam pohon dedalu tua; dalam sebagian kisah setempat ia dianggap padanan Leshy.
claims.quote: Rokita ( Polish: [rɔˈki.ta] ) is a demon in Polish folklore, that is said to inhabit the gateways to the underworld, including the wetlands, forests, and the insides of old willow trees. In some local tales, he is seen as an equivalent of Leshy.

claims.statement: The Romanian article also calls Rokita a devil of Polish folklore living in places linked with the gateway to the other world.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Rumania juga menyebut Rokita sebagai iblis dalam folklor Polandia yang tinggal di tempat-tempat yang dikaitkan dengan gerbang ke dunia lain.
claims.quote: Rokita este un diavol în folclorul polonez despre care se spune că locuiește în zone asociate cu poarta către lumea cealaltă

claims.statement: Rokita is the name of one of the devils of Polish folk legends; he has unimaginable strength but is not very cunning.
claims.statement_id: Rokita adalah nama salah satu iblis dalam legenda rakyat Polandia; ia memiliki kekuatan luar biasa tetapi tidak terlalu cerdik.
claims.quote: Rokita – imię jednego z diabłów, występującego w polskich podaniach ludowych. Cechuje go niewyobrażalna siła, ale za to nie jest zbyt przebiegły.

claims.statement: In Łęczyca depictions Rokita is often treated as an equivalent of Boruta, shown as a general in a golden cloak or wearing a hat and frock coat; there it was also believed he appears as a pig, bird, fish, horse, dog or mouse, and whatever his form he is hostile to people.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penggambaran dari Łęczyca, Rokita sering disamakan dengan Boruta dan digambarkan sebagai jenderal bermantel emas atau bertopi dan berjas panjang; di sana juga dipercaya ia muncul sebagai babi, burung, ikan, kuda, anjing, atau tikus, dan dalam wujud apa pun ia berniat jahat terhadap manusia.
claims.quote: W przedstawieniach łęczyckich Rokitę często traktują jako ekwiwalent Boruty, przedstawiają jako generała w złotym płaszczu bądź przyodziany w kapelusz oraz surdut. ... ukazuje się pod postaciami zwierzęcymi, takimi jak: świnia, ptak, ryba, koń, pies, mysz. Niezależnie od przybranej postaci czy to ludzkiej czy zwierzęcej cechują go wrogie intencje w stosunku do ludzi.

claims.statement: In another version of the legend, Rokita, also called Rokietnik, was an evil soul dwelling in bogs (his name coming from rokietnik moss, common in Central European forests) who drowned those who intruded on his territory.
claims.statement_id: Menurut versi legenda lain, Rokita yang juga disebut Rokietnik adalah jiwa jahat penghuni rawa (namanya dari lumut rokietnik yang umum di hutan Eropa Tengah) yang menenggelamkan orang yang masuk ke wilayahnya.
claims.quote: Według innej wersji legendy Rokita, zwany inaczej Rokietnikiem, był złą duszą zamieszkującą bagna (stąd jego nazwa pochodząca od mchu rokietnika często występującego w środkowoeuropejskich lasach) i topiącą tych, którzy wdarli się na teren jego siedliszcza.

claims.statement: Another legend tells that Rokita and Boruta went to an inn in Łódź to drink the local beer.
claims.statement_id: Legenda lain bercerita bahwa Rokita bersama Boruta pergi ke sebuah kedai di Łódź untuk minum bir setempat.
claims.quote: Kolejna z legend mówi, że Rokita razem z Borutą udali się do karczmy znajdującej się w Łodzi, aby napić się tamtejszego piwa.

claims.statement: Rokita was believed able to take the form of a cat, and witches in folk spells asked him especially for abundant cows giving more milk.
claims.statement_id: Rokita dipercaya bisa berwujud kucing, dan para penyihir dalam mantra rakyat terutama memintanya agar sapi-sapi memberi lebih banyak susu.
claims.quote: Wierzono, że potrafi przybierać postać kota. Czarownice w zaklęciach ludowych prosiły go szczególnie o obfitość krów, aby dawały więcej mleka.

claims.statement: In one legend, as a poor peasant wailed and wept, Rokita appeared before him and offered a great deal of money without interest, on condition it be repaid to the penny at a set day and hour, or else he would take his soul.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebuah legenda, ketika seorang petani miskin meratap dan menangis, Rokita muncul di hadapannya dan menawarkan banyak uang tanpa bunga, dengan syarat dikembalikan utuh pada hari dan jam yang ditentukan, kalau tidak jiwanya akan diambil.
