claims.quote: Gdy tak zawodził i płakał, stanął przed nim Rokita. ... Rokita ofiarował mu dużo pieniędzy, bez żadnego oprocentowania. Z warunkiem, że w ustalonym dniu oraz godzinie odda mu sumę co do grosza, w innym wypadku zabierze jego duszę.

claims.statement: Samca is an evil spirit of Romanian mythology who most often appears as a naked woman with dishevelled hair down to her heels, small eyes shining like stars, iron hands with long nails sharp as knitting needles or hooked like sickles, and a tongue of fire.
claims.statement_id: Samca adalah roh jahat dalam mitologi Rumania yang paling sering tampil sebagai perempuan telanjang berambut kusut hingga tumit, bermata kecil berkilau seperti bintang, bertangan besi dengan kuku panjang setajam jarum rajut atau melengkung seperti sabit, dan berlidah api.
claims.quote: Samca is an evil spirit in Romanian mythology. She most commonly takes the appearance of a naked woman with disheveled hair growing down to her heels, with small eyes that shine as brightly as the stars, with iron hands and long nails sharp as knitting needles or hooked as sickles and a tongue of fire.

claims.statement: Samca can also take the form of a huge fierce pig, a grinning dog with awful teeth, a hairless cat with fiery bulging eyes, a crow with bloody eyes and a big black spider.
claims.statement_id: Samca juga bisa berwujud babi besar yang ganas, anjing menyeringai dengan gigi mengerikan, kucing tak berbulu bermata menyala dan melotot, gagak bermata darah, dan laba-laba hitam besar.
claims.quote: Other forms Samca can take are: a very large and fierce pig, a grinning dog showing awful teeth, a hairless cat with fiery, bulging eyes, a crow with bloody eyes, and a big black spider.

claims.statement: It may come out at the end of each month, around full moon, usually appearing to children under four, who are so frightened they fall ill at once; the illness is called "the children's malice"; the demon can also appear to women about to give birth.
claims.statement_id: Ia bisa keluar pada akhir setiap bulan, sekitar bulan purnama, biasanya menampakkan diri kepada anak di bawah empat tahun yang begitu ketakutan hingga langsung sakit; penyakit itu disebut "kedengkian anak-anak"; demon ini juga muncul kepada perempuan yang akan melahirkan.
claims.quote: It can come out at the end of each month, around full moon, and it usually appears to children under the age of four, who are so frightened that they become sick immediately. The disease children develop after Samca appears to them is called "the children's malice". This demon can also appear to women who are about to give birth.

claims.statement: Samca has 19 names: Vestitia, Navadaraia, Valnomia, Sina, Nicosda, Avezuha, Scorcoila, Tiha, Miha, Grompa, Slalo, Necauza, Hatavu, Hulila, Huva, Ghiana, Gluviana, Prava and Samca; to protect themselves people must write all 19 names on a wall of the house.
claims.statement_id: Samca punya 19 nama: Vestitia, Navadaraia, Valnomia, Sina, Nicosda, Avezuha, Scorcoila, Tiha, Miha, Grompa, Slalo, Necauza, Hatavu, Hulila, Huva, Ghiana, Gluviana, Prava, dan Samca; untuk melindungi diri, orang harus menulis ke-19 nama itu di dinding rumah.
claims.quote: Samca has 19 names: Vestitia, Navadaraia, Valnomia, Sina, Nicosda, Avezuha, Scorcoila, Tiha, Miha, Grompa, Slalo, Necauza, Hatavu, Hulila, Huva, Ghiana, Gluviana, Prava, and Samca. To defend against Samca, people need to write all her 19 names on a wall of the house

claims.statement: Samca was described in 1900 by Rabbi Moses Gaster, who noted the similarity of Christian (Romanian, Greek, Slavonic) and Semitic (Aramaic) charms against child-stealing and how common these tales were in the Balkans; from a folk incantation recorded "from the mouth of the peasants of Roumania", Gaster called Samca Avezuha, the "wing of Satan".
claims.statement_id: Samca dideskripsikan pada 1900 oleh Rabbi Moses Gaster, yang mencatat kemiripan jimat Kristen (Rumania, Yunani, Slavonik) dan Semit (Aram) melawan pencurian anak serta seringnya kisah ini di Balkan; berdasarkan mantra rakyat dari "mulut para petani Rumania", Gaster menyebut Samca sebagai Avezuha, "sayap Setan".
claims.quote: The Samca was described in 1900 by Rabbi Moses Gaster, who noted the similarities between Christian (namely Romanian, Greek, and Slavonic) and Semitic (Aramaic) charms against child-stealing, and the frequency of these tales, both oral and written, in the Balkans. Per a folk incantation recorded from "the mouth of the peasants of Roumania", Gaster described Samca as Avezuha, the "wing of Satan".

claims.statement: The Romanian article calls Samca a figure of Romanian legends, an unclean spirit, very ugly and fierce.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Rumania menyebut Samca sebagai tokoh legenda Rumania, roh najis yang sangat buruk rupa dan ganas.
claims.quote: Samca este un personaj al legendelor românești, un spirit necurat, foarte urât și fioros

claims.statement: In tradition she is also linked in several legends with the End of the World, hedonism, sex and carnal pleasures, appearing in the dreams of young bridegrooms to tempt them to sin and betray their new wives.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi ia juga dikaitkan dalam beberapa legenda dengan Akhir Dunia, hedonisme, seks, dan kenikmatan jasmani, dan muncul dalam mimpi para pengantin pria muda untuk membujuk mereka berdosa dan mengkhianati istri baru mereka.
claims.quote: În tradiție ea este de asemenea asociată în mai multe legende cu Sfârșitul Lumii, cu hedonismul, sexul și plăcerile carnale. Ea le apărea în vis tinerilor miri în încercarea de a-i face să păcătuiască și să își însele proaspetele neveste.

claims.statement: In 2022 the Hamilton Fringe Festival new play contest was won by Natalia Bushnik and Kathleen Welch with their play Samca, which used the myth of Samca attacking pregnant women as a metaphor for abortion.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2022 lomba naskah baru Hamilton Fringe Festival dimenangkan Natalia Bushnik dan Kathleen Welch lewat drama Samca, yang memakai mitos Samca menyerang perempuan hamil sebagai metafora aborsi.
claims.quote: In 2022, Hamilton Fringe Festival's new play contest was won by playwrights Natalia Bushnik and Kathleen Welch for their play, Samca, which used the mythology of Samca attacking pregnant women as a metaphor for abortion.

claims.statement: The Sântoaderi were a group of supernatural beings of Romanian folklore, pictured as seven or nine young men with long feet and hooves, also thought to wear capes.
claims.statement_id: Sântoaderi adalah sekelompok makhluk gaib dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, dibayangkan sebagai tujuh atau sembilan pemuda berkaki panjang dan berkuku kuda (hooves), yang juga dianggap mengenakan jubah.
claims.quote: The Sântoaderi were a group of supernatural entities found in Romanian folklore. Viewed as either seven or nine young men with long feet and hooves, they were also thought of as wearing capes.

claims.statement: They were believed to appear mysteriously in a village, singing and beating drums, and to cause illness: wrapping people in chains, causing rheumatism, or stamping on their bodies.
claims.statement_id: Diyakini mereka muncul secara misterius di sebuah desa, bernyanyi, menabuh genderang, dan membuat orang sakit: membelit mereka dengan rantai sehingga terkena rematik, atau menginjak-injak tubuh mereka.
claims.quote: It was believed that they would mysteriously appear in a village, where they would sing, beat their drums, and cause illness for people; wrapping them up in chains causing rheumatism or stamping on their bodies.

claims.statement: On hearing their music and hoofbeats, people were advised to stay indoors, which was thought safe; those who did not could be kidnapped by the Sântoaderi and made part of their procession.
claims.statement_id: Begitu mendengar musik dan derap kuku mereka, orang dianjurkan tetap di dalam rumah, yang dianggap aman; yang tidak masuk rumah bisa diculik Sântoaderi dan dijadikan bagian dari arak-arakan mereka.
claims.quote: Upon hearing their music and the sound of hooves, people were advised to stay indoors, which was considered safe. Those that did not retreat indoors, could be kidnapped by the Sântoaderi and made part of the procession.

claims.statement: Victims of such kidnappings sometimes came back healthy and carrying gifts, and at other times sick, dying or insane.
claims.statement_id: Korban penculikan itu kadang kembali dalam keadaan sehat sambil membawa hadiah, kadang kembali dalam keadaan sakit, sekarat, atau gila.
claims.quote: The victims of such kidnappings would sometimes return in healthy condition and carrying gifts; other times, they would return sick, dying, or insane.

claims.statement: The name "Sântoader" derives from a regional name for Saint Theodore, and folklore holds that the creatures were more likely to appear on his feast day.
claims.statement_id: Nama "Sântoader" berasal dari sebutan daerah untuk Santo Theodorus, dan menurut cerita rakyat makhluk ini lebih mungkin muncul pada hari rayanya.
claims.quote: The name "Sântoader" derives from a regional name for Saint Theodore, with folklore suggesting that the creatures were more likely to appear on his feast day.

claims.statement: The Sântoaderi share some similarities with the fairies of Irish folklore; the Romanian historian Mircea Eliade also noted a resemblance between the Sântoaderi and the zîne, the Romanian equivalent of the fairy godmother.
claims.statement_id: Sântoaderi memiliki beberapa kemiripan dengan peri dalam cerita rakyat Irlandia; sejarawan Rumania Mircea Eliade juga mencatat kemiripan antara Sântoaderi dan zîne, padanan Rumania untuk ibu peri.
claims.quote: The Sântoaderi share some similarities with the fairies of Irish folklore. The Romanian historian Mircea Eliade also noted a similarity between the Sântoaderi and the zîne, the Romanian equivalent of the fairy godmother

claims.statement: The Romanian article describes the Sântoaderi as a group of supernatural entities in Romanian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Rumania menyebut Sântoaderi sebagai sekelompok entitas gaib dalam folklor Rumania.
claims.quote: Sântoaderii sunt un grup de entități supranaturale din folclorul românesc.

claims.statement: There is also a belief that on the 24th day after Easter (a 24-a zi după Paște) the zânele și Sântoaderii, that is the zâne and the Sântoaderi, meet to play and give each other bouquets of flowers.
claims.statement_id: Ada pula kepercayaan bahwa pada hari ke-24 setelah Paskah (a 24-a zi după Paște), zânele și Sântoaderii, yaitu para zâne dan Sântoaderi, bertemu untuk bermain dan saling memberi karangan bunga.
claims.quote: Există, de asemenea, credința că în a 24-a zi după Paște, zânele și Sântoaderii se întâlnesc pentru a se juca și a-și oferi buchete de flori.

claims.statement: The Romanian historian of religions Mircea Eliade noted a resemblance between the Sântoaderi and the zâne, who were also believed to travel by night in a procession of dancers.
claims.statement_id: Sejarawan agama Rumania Mircea Eliade mencatat kemiripan antara Sântoaderi dan zâne, yang juga dipercaya berkelana pada malam hari dalam arak-arakan penari.
claims.quote: Istoricul român al religiilor Mircea Eliade a remarcat o asemănare între Sântoaderi și zâne, despre care se credea că, de asemenea, călătoresc noaptea într-un cortegiu de dansatoare.

claims.statement: The Sea Tsar is a character of East Slavic folktales and bylinas (oral epics), the tsar of the sea realms; the best-known examples are the bylinas about Sadko and the fairy tales about Vasilisa the Wise, such as The Sea Tsar and Vasilisa the Wise.
claims.statement_id: Tsar Laut adalah tokoh dalam dongeng dan bylina (epos lisan) Slavia Timur, raja alam laut; contoh paling terkenal adalah bylina tentang Sadko dan dongeng tentang Vasilisa yang Bijak, seperti The Sea Tsar and Vasilisa the Wise.
claims.quote: is a character in East Slavic folktales and bylinas, the tsar of the sea realms. The best known examples are bylinas about Sadko and fairy tales about Vasilisa the Wise, such as The Sea Tsar and Vasilisa the Wise.

claims.statement: Vsevolod Miller suggested that the image of the Sea Tsar was influenced by the Finnish god Ahti, known to the pomors (seashore dwellers of the Russian North).
claims.statement_id: Vsevolod Miller berpendapat bahwa gambaran Tsar Laut dipengaruhi dewa Finlandia Ahti, yang dikenal oleh kaum pomor (penghuni pesisir di Rusia Utara).
claims.quote: Vsevolod Miller suggested that the image of the Sea Tsar was influenced by the Finnish god Ahti, known for the pomors (Russian seashore dwellers of the Russian North).

claims.statement: Miller also doubted that the Sea Tsar of these tales reflects old East Slavic pagan belief, and thought it was probably based on the tales of itinerant storytellers.
claims.statement_id: Miller juga meragukan bahwa gambaran Tsar Laut dalam dongeng-dongeng ini mencerminkan kepercayaan pagan Slavia Timur kuno; menurutnya gambaran itu mungkin berasal dari kisah para pencerita keliling.
claims.quote: Also Miller doubted that the image of Sea Tsar in these fairy tales reflects old East Slavic pagan beliefs and is probably based on the tales of itinerary storytellers.

claims.statement: The Sea Tsar should not be confused with the water spirit vodyanoy.
claims.statement_id: Tsar Laut tidak boleh dikacaukan dengan roh air vodyanoy.
claims.quote: The Sea Tsar should not be confused with the water spirit, vodyanoy.

claims.statement: Some draw a parallel between the Sea Tsar and the tale of the South Slavic morski kralj (sea king) recorded, for example, by the Slovenian poet and ethnologist Matija Valjavec.
claims.statement_id: Sebagian orang menyejajarkan Tsar Laut dengan kisah morski kralj (raja laut) Slavia Selatan yang dicatat antara lain oleh penyair dan etnolog Slovenia Matija Valjavec.
claims.quote: Some draw the parallel of the Sea Tsar with the tale about South Slavic morski kralj recorded, e.g., by Slovenian poet and ethnologist Matija Valjavec

claims.statement: The Russian article calls him a character of Russian folktales and bylinas: master of the sea floor, lord of all waters, ruler of the underwater dwellers and owner of countless treasures; he is also called Царь Водяник, Поддонный царь and Заморский царь.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Rusia menyebutnya tokoh dongeng dan bylina rakyat Rusia: tuan dasar laut, penguasa semua perairan, raja para penghuni bawah air, dan pemilik harta tak terhitung; ia juga disebut Царь Водяник, Поддонный царь, dan Заморский царь.
claims.quote: персонаж русских народных сказок и былин: хозяин дна морского, повелитель всех вод, владыка над подводными обитателями, владелец несметных сокровищ.

claims.statement: The Sea Tsar's palace of crystal, silver, gold and precious stones is placed vaguely: now in the blue sea, now on an island, now in Lake Ilmen; when he dances and makes merry, the sea storms and a tempest rises.
claims.statement_id: Istana Tsar Laut dari kristal, perak, emas, dan batu permata letaknya tidak tetap: kadang di laut biru, kadang di sebuah pulau, kadang di Danau Ilmen; ketika ia menari dan bersenang-senang, laut bergolak dan badai pun datang.
claims.quote: Дворец Морского царя, сделанный из хрусталя, серебра, золота и драгоценных камней, помещается неопределённо: то в синем море, то на острове, то в Ильмень-озере. Когда он пляшет и развлекается — на море шторм и поднимается буря.

claims.statement: He loves merrymaking and summons drowned musicians to his palace, where they play and the water tsar dances to their music.
claims.statement_id: Ia suka bersenang-senang, sehingga memanggil para musisi yang tenggelam ke istananya; mereka bermain musik dan raja air itu menari mengikuti musiknya.
claims.quote: Он любит повеселиться, для чего утонувших музыкантов созывает к себе во дворец, где музыканты начинают играть, а водяной царь пляшет под их музыку.

claims.statement: In the bylinas he first creates Sadko's wealth and then, once Sadko has grown rich, demands that he come to his underwater kingdom.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bylina, ia mula-mula membuat Sadko kaya, lalu setelah Sadko kaya ia menuntut Sadko datang ke kerajaan bawah lautnya.
claims.quote: В былинах он сначала создаёт богатство Садко, а потом, когда Садко разбогател, требует его к себе в подводное царство.

claims.statement: In the tale of Vasilisa the Wise he likewise wants to keep the hero (Ivan-tsarevich) in his underwater kingdom, but his daughter Vasilisa, who has fallen in love with the prince, flees with him and saves him from her father's pursuit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng Vasilisa yang Bijak, ia juga ingin menahan sang pahlawan (Ivan-tsarevich) di kerajaan bawah lautnya, tetapi putrinya, Vasilisa, yang jatuh cinta kepada sang pangeran, melarikan diri bersamanya dan menyelamatkannya dari kejaran sang ayah.
claims.quote: Здесь он также хочет оставить у себя в подводном царстве героя (Ивана-царевича), но полюбившая царевича дочь морского царя, Василиса, убегает вместе с ним и спасает его от погони отца.

claims.statement: The vodyanoy, with bloated bellies and swollen faces, living in pools especially near mills, drinking, playing dice, stealing horses and cows and drowning people, are wholly different from the Sea Tsar of the bylinas, who lives in rich halls and is portrayed as a passionate lover of music.
claims.statement_id: Para vodyanoy berperut gembung dan berwajah bengkak yang tinggal di lubuk dekat penggilingan, mabuk-mabukan, main dadu, mencuri kuda dan sapi, serta menenggelamkan orang, sama sekali berbeda dengan Tsar Laut bylina yang tinggal di istana mewah dan digambarkan sebagai pencinta musik.
claims.quote: Эти водяные, с одутловатым брюхом и опухшим лицом, живущие в омутах, особенно около мельниц, известные пьяницы, посещающие кабаки, играющие в кости, ворующие лошадей и коров и топящие людей, — совершенно отличны от былинного морского царя, который живёт в богатых палатах и изображается страстным любителем музыки.

claims.statement: Shatans are odd-looking creatures of Belarusian folklore; they are neutral characters who act as symbols of idleness and laziness.
claims.statement_id: Shatan adalah makhluk berpenampilan aneh dalam cerita rakyat Belarus; mereka tokoh netral yang menjadi lambang kemalasan.
claims.quote: are odd-looking creatures of Belarusian folklore. Shatans are neutral characters and act as symbols of idleness and laziness.

claims.statement: Shatans are very annoying to others and lead them into the same useless wandering; they cannot communicate normally with anyone, even each other, and do not help one another in trouble.
claims.statement_id: Shatan sangat mengganggu orang lain dan mendorong mereka ikut berkelana tanpa guna; mereka tidak bisa berkomunikasi dengan normal, bahkan dengan sesamanya, dan tidak saling menolong saat kesulitan.
claims.quote: Shatans are very annoying for other people and dispose them to the same way of useless wandering. Shatans cannot communicate with anyone in a normal way, even with each other, and in case of trouble they don't rescue and help one another.

claims.statement: Belarusian folklore says that angry folk creatures (the witch, for example) tease shatans, and since shatans are cowardly they hide or run from their tormentors.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Belarus disebutkan bahwa makhluk-makhluk pemarah (misalnya penyihir) mengganggu shatan, dan karena shatan dikenal penakut, mereka bersembunyi atau lari dari pengganggunya.
claims.quote: In Belarusian folklore it is said that angry folkloric creatures (for example, the witch) tease shatans. As shatans are also known as cowardly creatures which hide or run away from offenders.

claims.statement: When tired of wandering, shatans sometimes weave bast shoes, which quickly wear out from their useless wandering.
claims.statement_id: Ketika lelah berkelana, shatan kadang menganyam sepatu kulit kayu (lapti), yang cepat aus karena pengembaraan mereka yang sia-sia.
claims.quote: When shatans are tired of wandering around, they sometimes spin bast shoes. Bast shoes are quickly worn away because of the shatans' useless wandering.

claims.statement: Shatans are Belarusian mythological characters described by Nikolai Nikiforovsky in his work on the folk tales of unclean spirits in Vitebsk Belarus.
claims.statement_id: Shatan adalah tokoh mitologi Belarus yang dideskripsikan oleh Nikolai Nikiforovsky dalam karyanya tentang kisah-kisah rakyat mengenai kekuatan najis di Belarus wilayah Vitebsk.
claims.quote: белорусские мифологические персонажи, описанные Николаем Никифоровским в работе «Нечистики. Свод простонародных в Витебской Белоруссии сказаний о нечистой силе».

claims.statement: Shatans can roam aimlessly all day along roads, fields and forests without doing anything useful.
claims.statement_id: Shatan bisa seharian berkeliaran tanpa tujuan di jalan, ladang, dan hutan tanpa melakukan apa pun yang berguna.
claims.quote: Шатаны могут целыми днями бесцельно бродить по дорогам, полям, лесам, не делая ничего полезного.

claims.statement: In a certain mythological dictionary, the word «шатана» is given as a synonym for Satan.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kamus mitologi tertentu, kata «шатана» dicantumkan sebagai sinonim untuk setan.
claims.quote: В «Мифологическом словаре» слово «шатана» приведено как синоним сатаны.

claims.statement: They smoke foul-smelling tobacco and growl at one another; you will wait in vain for a smile or a kind word from them.
claims.statement_id: Mereka mengisap tembakau berbau busuk dan saling menggeram; tak ada senyum atau kata baik yang bisa ditunggu dari mereka.
claims.quote: Яны паляць смуродны тытунь і гыркаюць адзін на аднаго. Ні ўсмешкі, ні добрага слова ад іх не дачакаешся.

claims.statement: When tired of constant walking, shatans sometimes weave bast shoes and make themselves sticks, but the shoes soon wear out and the sticks break from their endless useless roaming.
claims.statement_id: Saat lelah berjalan terus, shatan kadang menganyam lapti dan membuat tongkat, tetapi lapti cepat aus dan tongkat patah karena pengembaraan mereka yang sia-sia.
claims.quote: Калі Шатаны стамляюцца ад пастаяннага хаджэнні, яны часам плятуць лапці і робяць сабе кіі. Лапці хутка сціраюцца, а кіі ламаюцца ад пастаянна бескарыснага бадзяння.

claims.statement: In Albanian mythology the shtojzovalle (also shtojzorreshta or shtozote) is a small creature with supernatural powers and extraordinary beauty; they are invisible woodland creatures, rarely seen by humans, fond of song and dance.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Albania, shtojzovalle (juga disebut shtojzorreshta atau shtozote) adalah makhluk kecil berkekuatan gaib dan sangat elok; mereka makhluk hutan yang tak kasatmata, jarang terlihat manusia, dan gemar bernyanyi serta menari.
claims.quote: In Albanian mythology, the shtojzovalle, also known as shtojzorreshta, shtozote is a small creature with supernatural powers and of extraordinary beauty. They are invisible woodland creatures, which can be seen by humans only on rare occasions and are fond of song and dance.

claims.statement: The term shtojzovalle derives from the Albanian shtoj (add), zot (god, deity) and valle (dance), meaning "may God give increase to their dance".
claims.statement_id: Istilah shtojzovalle berasal dari kata Albania shtoj (menambah), zot (Tuhan, dewa), dan valle (tarian), sehingga berarti "semoga Tuhan menambah tarian mereka".
claims.quote: The term shtojzovalle derives from the Albanian words shtoj (English: add), zot (English: god, deity) and valle (English: dance), with the term meaning in English "may God give increase to their dance"

claims.statement: They live in forests and pastures, spend their time singing and dancing, can fly, and at night spin the thread of human existence; a human can see them only by lifting an invisible veil before their eyes.
claims.statement_id: Mereka tinggal di hutan dan padang rumput, menghabiskan waktu dengan bernyanyi dan menari, mampu terbang, dan pada malam hari memintal benang kehidupan manusia; manusia hanya bisa melihat mereka jika mengangkat selubung tak kasatmata di depan matanya.
claims.quote: They live in forests and pastures and spend their time singing and dancing. They have the ability to fly and at night they spin the thread of human existence. They are invisible to humans and a human can see them only if they lift an invisible veil in front of their eyes.

claims.statement: Humans and shtojzovalles occasionally marry, but a man can keep a shtojzovalle maiden only if he gives her his clothes to wear.
claims.statement_id: Kadang manusia dan shtojzovalle menikah, tetapi seorang lelaki hanya dapat mempertahankan gadis shtojzovalle jika ia memberikan pakaiannya untuk dikenakan sang gadis.
claims.quote: Occasionally humans and shtojzovalles are married, but a human can keep a shtojzovalle maiden only if he gives her his clothes to wear.

claims.statement: If a human builds a house on land inhabited by shtojzovalles, it will be haunted by shtojzovalles shaking heavy iron chains; people who step on a shtojzovalle while walking may be devoured by it.
claims.statement_id: Jika manusia membangun rumah di tanah yang dihuni shtojzovalle, rumah itu akan dihantui shtojzovalle yang mengguncang rantai besi berat; orang yang menginjak shtojzovalle saat berjalan bisa dimangsa olehnya.
claims.quote: If a human builds their house on lands inhabited by shtojzovalles, the house will be haunted by shtojzovalles shaking heavy iron chains. When people go for a walk and step on a shtojzovalle they may get devoured by it.

claims.statement: Albanian Christians, especially the Catholics of northern Albania and Malësia, gave the shtojzovalles Christian features: in these traditions, when Archangel Michael fought Satan, the angels who stayed neutral became the shtojzovalles.
claims.statement_id: Umat Kristen Albania, terutama umat Katolik di Albania utara dan Malësia, memberi shtojzovalle beberapa ciri Kristen: menurut tradisi ini, ketika Malaikat Agung Mikael melawan Setan, para malaikat yang tetap netral menjadi shtojzovalle.
claims.quote: Albanian Christians and especially the Catholics of northern Albania and Malësia have attributed several Christian characteristics to the shtojzovalles. According to these traditions when Archangel Michael fought against Satan the angels who remained neutral became the shtojzovalles.

claims.statement: The shtojzovalles weep in repentance for their neutrality, and a human on whom their tears fall will die; the Albanian phrase i ka rënë pika ("a drop fell upon him"), a figure of speech for someone's death, comes from this belief.
claims.statement_id: Shtojzovalle menangis menyesali kenetralan mereka, dan jika air mata mereka jatuh ke manusia, orang itu akan mati; ungkapan Albania i ka rënë pika ("setetes jatuh padanya"), kiasan untuk kematian seseorang, berasal dari kepercayaan ini.
claims.quote: The shtojzovalles weep in repentance for their neutrality and if their tears fall on a human he will die. The Albanian phrase i ka rënë pika (English: "a drop fell upon him"), metaphorically means that someone died and the phrase is derived from this belief.

claims.statement: The name shtojzovalle is a product of pagan and Christian religious syncretism; the alternative term shtojzorreshta means "may God give increase to their rows".
claims.statement_id: Nama shtojzovalle merupakan hasil sinkretisme agama pagan dan Kristen; istilah lain, shtojzorreshta, berarti "semoga Tuhan menambah barisan mereka".
claims.quote: The name shtojzovalle is a product of Pagan and Christian religious syncretism. The alternative term shtojzorreshta means "may God give increase to their rows" in English.

claims.statement: The Spanish article calls it a small dancing and singing creature of both sexes, of great beauty and supernatural powers, from Albanian mythology, living in mountains and dense forests.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Spanyol menyebutnya makhluk kecil penari dan penyanyi dari kedua jenis kelamin, sangat elok dan berkekuatan gaib, dalam mitologi Albania, yang tinggal di gunung dan hutan lebat.
claims.quote: es una criaturilla danzarina y cantarina de ambos sexos de gran belleza y poderes sobrenaturales de la mitología albanesa. Habita en montes y bosques densos.

claims.statement: The Albanian article describes the shtojzovallet as small male and female beings of extraordinary beauty who live in forests and pastures and spend their time singing and dancing.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Albania menyebut shtojzovallet sebagai makhluk kecil lelaki dan perempuan yang sangat elok, tinggal di hutan dan padang rumput, dan menghabiskan waktu dengan bernyanyi dan menari.
claims.quote: Shtojzovallet janë krijesa të vogla mashkullore dhe femërore me bukuri të jashtëzakonshme. Ato jetojnë në pyje dhe kullota dhe kalojnë kohën duke kënduar dhe duke vallëzuar.

claims.statement: Szélatya (also Szélkirály; Old Turkic Çel Ede or Çel Ata, "Wind Father") is the Turkic god of wind.
claims.statement_id: Szélatya (juga Szélkirály; dalam bahasa Turk Kuno Çel Ede atau Çel Ata, "Bapa Angin") adalah dewa angin bangsa Turk.
claims.quote: is the Turkic god or deity of wind.

claims.statement: In Azerbaijani his name is Yel ata or Yel baba.
claims.statement_id: Dalam bahasa Azerbaijan namanya Yel ata atau Yel baba.
claims.quote: Azerbaijani: Yel ata / Yel baba

claims.statement: Szelatya has long hair, silver weapons and thunder horses; in Hungarian mythology he appears as a handsome young man, but in Turkic mythology as an old man; he has a forest called the Silver Forest.
claims.statement_id: Szelatya berambut panjang, bersenjata perak, dan memiliki kuda guntur; dalam mitologi Hungaria ia tampil sebagai pemuda tampan, tetapi dalam mitologi Turk sebagai lelaki tua; ia memiliki hutan bernama Hutan Perak.
claims.quote: Szelatya has long hair, silver weapons, and thunder horses. He is said to appear as a youthful and handsome man in Hungarian mythology, but as an elderly man in Turkic mythology. He has a jungle or sylvan named Silver Forest.

claims.statement: His father is Arany Atyacska (Golden Father) and his mother Hajnal Anyacska (Dawn Mother), though some accounts make him the son of Kayra, the primordial god.
claims.statement_id: Ayahnya Arany Atyacska (Bapa Emas) dan ibunya Hajnal Anyacska (Ibu Fajar), tetapi beberapa kisah menyebutnya putra Kayra, dewa purba.
claims.quote: His father is Arany Atyacska (Golden Father) and his mother's name is Hajnal Anyacska (Dawn Mother). However, some accounts mention that he is the son of Kayra, the primordial god.

claims.statement: His female counterpart is Szélanya.
claims.statement_id: Padanan perempuannya adalah Szélanya.
claims.quote: His female counterpart is Szélanya.

claims.statement: The Serbian article calls Szélatya and Szélkirály the god of wind in Hungarian mythology (мађарској митологији).
claims.statement_id: Artikel Serbia menyebut Szélatya dan Szélkirály sebagai dewa angin dalam mitologi Hungaria (мађарској митологији).
claims.quote: је у мађарској митологији бог и божанство ветра.

claims.statement: The Onoghurs also worshipped him.
claims.statement_id: Bangsa Onoghur juga memujanya.
claims.quote: The Onoghurs also worshipped him.

claims.statement: The Turkish article calls Yel Ata the wind god in Turkic, Altai, Tatar and Hungarian mythologies, also called Cel (Çel, Şil, Cil) Ata.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Turki menyebut Yel Ata sebagai dewa angin dalam mitologi Turk, Altai, Tatar, dan Hungaria, yang juga disebut Cel (Çel, Şil, Cil) Ata.
claims.quote: Yel Ata - Türk, Altay, Tatar ve Macar mitolojilerinde rüzgâr tanrısı. Cel (Çel, Şil, Cil) Ata da denir.

claims.statement: Yel Ata is the god ruling all the world's storms, winds, whirlwinds, tornadoes and typhoons; villagers who want to winnow their threshing call on Yel Ata for help.
claims.statement_id: Yel Ata adalah dewa penguasa semua badai, angin, puting beliung, dan taifun di dunia; para petani yang hendak menampi hasil panen memanggilnya untuk membantu.
claims.quote: Dünyadaki tüm fırtınaların, rüzgârların, kasırgaların, hortumların, tayfunların yöneticisi olan tanrıdır. Harman savurmak isteyen köylüler Yel Ata'yı yardıma çağırırlar.

claims.statement: They cry "Yel Ata, gel atına saman götür..." ("Yel Ata, come, take straw for your horse"), and he comes and winnows the threshing so he can carry straw for his horse.
claims.statement_id: Mereka berseru "Yel Ata, gel atına saman götür..." ("Yel Ata, datanglah, bawakan jerami untuk kudamu"), dan ia datang menampi panen agar bisa membawa jerami untuk kudanya.
claims.quote: "Yel Ata, gel atına saman götür..." diye bağırırlar, o da atına saman götürebilmek için gelip harmanı savurur.

claims.statement: The word derives from the root Yel/Yil/İl/Zel/Cel, meaning a breeze.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini diturunkan dari akar Yel/Yil/İl/Zel/Cel, yang berarti hembusan angin.
claims.quote: (Yel/Yil/İl/Zel/Cel) kökünden türemiştir. Esinti anlamı vardır.

claims.statement: The Dragon of the North or Northern Frog is a legendary frog-like creature of Estonian lore; the story was popularised by Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald in the collection Eesti rahva ennemuistsed jutud (Old Tales of the Estonian People, 1866).
claims.statement_id: Naga dari Utara atau Katak Utara adalah makhluk legenda mirip katak dalam cerita rakyat Estonia; kisahnya dipopulerkan Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald dalam kumpulan Eesti rahva ennemuistsed jutud (Old Tales of the Estonian People, 1866).
claims.quote: is a legendary frog-like creature in Estonian lore. The story was popularized by Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald in the collection Eesti rahva ennemuistsed jutud or Old Tales of the Estonian People (1866).

claims.statement: The frog is described as a massive, dragon-like monster that wreaks havoc on the land until it is defeated.
claims.statement_id: Katak itu digambarkan sebagai monster raksasa mirip naga yang memorakporandakan negeri sampai akhirnya dikalahkan.
claims.quote: The frog is described as a massive, dragon-like monster that wreaks havoc on the land until it is defeated.

claims.statement: In the tale, a terrible monster came out of the North, laying waste whole tracts of country and devouring both men and beasts.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah itu, sesosok monster mengerikan datang dari Utara, menghancurkan wilayah-wilayah luas dan memangsa manusia serta hewan.
claims.quote: there lived a terrible monster, who came out of the North, and laid waste whole tracts of country, devouring both men and beasts

claims.statement: The frog's body was covered with scales stronger than stone and iron, so nothing could harm it, and its two large eyes shone night and day like the brightest candles.
claims.statement_id: Tubuh katak itu tertutup sisik yang lebih kuat dari batu dan besi sehingga tak ada yang bisa melukainya, dan kedua mata besarnya bersinar siang dan malam seperti lilin paling terang.
claims.quote: "The frog's body was completely covered with scales, which were stronger than stone and iron, so that nothing could harm it. Its two large eyes shone night and day like the brightest candles..."

claims.statement: The frog appeared in "Põhja Konn" (literally "The Northern Frog") by Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald.
claims.statement_id: Katak ini muncul dalam kisah "Põhja Konn" (harfiah "Katak Utara") karya Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald.
claims.quote: The frog appeared in "Põhja Konn" (literally "The Northern Frog") by Friedrich Reinhold Kreutzwald

claims.statement: In it Kreutzwald tells of a young man who obtains and uses a signet ring to defeat the monstrous beast.
claims.statement_id: Di dalamnya Kreutzwald menceritakan seorang pemuda yang memperoleh dan memakai sebuah cincin meterai untuk mengalahkan binatang raksasa itu.
claims.quote: In it, Kreutzwald tells the story of a young man who acquires and uses a signet ring to defeat a monstrous beast.

claims.statement: The story became internationally known when included in Andrew Lang and Leonora Blanche Lang's The Yellow Fairy Book (1894) as "The Dragon of the North".
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini dikenal internasional setelah dimuat dalam The Yellow Fairy Book (1894) karya Andrew Lang dan Leonora Blanche Lang dengan judul "The Dragon of the North".
claims.quote: It also gained international recognition when included in Andrew Lang and Leonora Blanche Lang's The Yellow Fairy Book (1894) under the title "The Dragon of the North."

claims.statement: The Estonian scholar Risto Järv classes the Northern Frog as a variant of the dragon-slayer tale (ATU 300) in the Aarne–Thompson–Uther Index, with the frog replacing the dragon as an oicotype.
claims.statement_id: Sarjana Estonia Risto Järv menggolongkan Katak Utara sebagai varian kisah pembunuh naga (ATU 300) dalam Indeks Aarne–Thompson–Uther, dengan katak menggantikan naga sebagai oikotipe (versi lokal).
claims.quote: Estonian scholar Risto Järv classifies the Northern Frog as a variant of a dragon-slayer (ATU 300) using the Aarne–Thompson–Uther Index, with the frog replacing the dragon and functioning as an oicotype

claims.statement: According to August Annist, in adapting a dragon-slayer story to the Estonian setting, Kreutzwald made the dragon frog-like.
claims.statement_id: Menurut August Annist, ketika menyesuaikan kisah pembunuh naga dengan konteks Estonia, Kreutzwald membuat naganya mirip katak.
claims.quote: According to August Annist, in adapting a dragonslayer style of story to the Estonian context, Kreutzwald made the dragon frog-like.

claims.statement: In the 2007 novel The Man Who Spoke Snakish, Andrus Kivirähk depicts the Northern Frog as a giant, dormant protector of the Estonians against Christian crusaders.
claims.statement_id: Dalam novel 2007 The Man Who Spoke Snakish, Andrus Kivirähk menggambarkan Katak Utara sebagai pelindung raksasa bangsa Estonia yang tertidur, melawan tentara salib Kristen.
claims.quote: In the 2007 novel, The Man Who Spoke Snakish, author Andrus Kivirähk depicts the Northern Frog as a giant, dormant protector of the Estonians against Christian crusaders.

claims.statement: In 2025 the artist Navitrolla installed the Tamula konn statue at Tamula Beach in Võru, explicitly drawing on the Northern Frog legend and presenting the frog as a protector.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2025 seniman Navitrolla memasang patung Tamula konn di Pantai Tamula, Võru, yang secara terang mengambil legenda Katak Utara dan menempatkan katak itu sebagai pelindung.
claims.quote: In 2025, the artist Navitrolla installed a statue in Võru at Tamula Beach called the Tamula konn that explicitly draws on the legend of the Northern Frog. Navitrolla positions the frog as a protector.

claims.statement: Andrew Lang included it in The Yellow Fairy Book, citing as his source "Der Norlands Drache" from Ehstnische Märchen, F. Löwe's German translation of Kreutzwald's work.
claims.statement_id: Andrew Lang memasukkannya ke The Yellow Fairy Book dan mencantumkan sumbernya "Der Norlands Drache" dari Ehstnische Märchen, terjemahan Jerman karya Kreutzwald oleh F. Löwe.
claims.quote: Isinama ito ni Andrew Lang sa The Yellow Fairy Book; inilista niya ang kaniyang pinagmulan bilang "Der Norlands Drache" mula sa Ehstnische Märchen, na salin sa Aleman ng gawa ni Kreutzwald, ni F. Löwe.

claims.statement: The youth went to the kingdom where a king offered his daughter and half his kingdom to whoever could kill the dragon.
claims.statement_id: Sang pemuda pergi ke kerajaan tempat seorang raja menawarkan putrinya dan separuh kerajaannya kepada siapa pun yang bisa membunuh sang naga.
claims.quote: Pumunta siya sa kaharian kung saan inalok ng isang hari ang kaniyang anak na babae at kalahati ng kaniyang kaharian sa sinumang makapatay ng dragon

claims.statement: According to Slavic folklore, the unclean dead are those who died an unnatural death and found no peace afterwards; they were believed to return to the world of the living and go on existing on earth as malevolent mythical beings.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat Slavia, arwah najis adalah orang yang mati secara tidak wajar dan tidak menemukan kedamaian setelah mati; mereka dipercaya kembali ke dunia orang hidup dan melanjutkan keberadaan di bumi sebagai makhluk mitos yang jahat.
claims.quote: The unclean dead, according to Slavic folklore, are those who died an unnatural death and did not find peace after death. They were believed to return to the world of the living and continue their existence on earth as malevolent mythical beings.

claims.statement: Russian ethnography also uses the term zalozhnye pokoiniki (заложные покойники), introduced into scholarship in the early 20th century by the ethnographer Dmitry Zelenin.
claims.statement_id: Dalam etnografi Rusia dipakai pula istilah zalozhnye pokoiniki (заложные покойники), yang diperkenalkan ke dunia ilmiah pada awal abad ke-20 oleh etnografer Dmitry Zelenin.
claims.quote: In Russian ethnography, the term zalozhnye pokoiniki (Russian: заложные покойники ) is also used

claims.statement: It was believed that the soul of a "restless" dead person could not pass into the afterlife and so wandered the earth, and that such dead could turn into malevolent spirits.
claims.statement_id: Diyakini bahwa jiwa orang mati yang "tak tenang" tidak bisa pergi ke alam baka sehingga mengembara di bumi, dan orang mati semacam itu bisa berubah menjadi roh jahat.
claims.quote: It was believed that the soul of a so-called "restless" (Russian: неупокоенный ) dead could not pass on to the afterlife and therefore wandered the earth. According to Slavic folklore, such dead could turn into malevolent spirits.

claims.statement: They were buried outside church grounds, at places such as crossroads, field boundaries, forests, swamps or ravines, because they were believed to be "cursed by their parents, and the earth would not receive them".
claims.statement_id: Mereka dikuburkan di luar lingkungan gereja, misalnya di persimpangan jalan, batas ladang, hutan, rawa, atau jurang, karena dipercaya "dikutuk orang tua mereka dan bumi tidak mau menerima mereka".
claims.quote: Rather, they were buried outside the territory of a church, in places such as at crossroads, field boundaries, forests, swamps, or ravines, since it was believed that they were "cursed by their parents and the earth would not receive them."

claims.statement: "Zalozhny dead" were typically those who died violently, suicides, those who died of drink, the drowned, unbaptised children, sorcerers and witches.
claims.statement_id: Yang biasanya dianggap "zalozhny" adalah orang yang mati karena kekerasan, bunuh diri, mati karena mabuk, mati tenggelam, anak yang belum dibaptis, dukun, dan penyihir.
claims.quote: "Zalozhny dead" were typically considered to be those who died violently, suicides, drunken deaths, drowning victims, unbaptized children, sorcerers, and witches.

claims.statement: Zelenin linked the origin of the word "zalozhny" to the burial method: the body was laid face down in the coffin and the grave sealed with stones and branches.
claims.statement_id: Zelenin mengaitkan asal kata "zalozhny" dengan cara penguburannya: jasad diletakkan telungkup di dalam peti dan kuburnya ditutup dengan batu dan ranting.
claims.quote: He linked the origin of the word “zalozhny” to the burial method itself: the body was placed face down in the coffin, and the grave was sealed with stones and branches

claims.statement: The Russian article describes заложные покойники as people who, in Slavic belief, died an unnatural death and found no rest after death.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Rusia menyebut заложные покойники sebagai orang yang menurut kepercayaan Slavia mati tidak wajar dan tidak mendapat ketenangan setelah mati.
claims.quote: по славянским верованиям, умершие неестественной смертью люди, не получившие после смерти успокоения.

claims.statement: In Simbirsk Governorate it was believed that during a drought one had to find a drunkard whom the earth would not accept, dig him up and throw him into a swamp so that rain would come.
claims.statement_id: Di Kegubernuran Simbirsk ada kepercayaan bahwa saat kemarau orang harus menemukan pemabuk yang tidak diterima bumi, menggalinya, dan membuangnya ke rawa agar hujan turun.
claims.quote: В Симбирской губернии существовало поверье, что во время засухи «надо непременно найти опойца, которого не принимает земля, поэтому его надо вырыть из земли и кинуть в болото, чтобы пошёл дождь».

claims.statement: There is a legend of Baturka, believed to be very greedy, so that passers-by had to leave an offering or he might bring disease on them and their livestock.
claims.statement_id: Ada legenda tentang Baturka yang dipercaya sangat rakus, sehingga orang yang lewat harus meninggalkan persembahan; kalau tidak, ia bisa mendatangkan penyakit kepada mereka dan ternaknya.
claims.quote: Известна, например, легенда о Батурке, который по поверью был очень жадным, поэтому, чтобы утолить его алчность, проходящие мимо люди должны были сделать подношение, иначе он мог нагнать на них и их скот болезнь.

claims.statement: In Belarus places of violent death were considered unclean, and passers-by threw stones, branches, a tuft of straw or a handful of earth onto them, "or else the dead man will chase them for a long time".
claims.statement_id: Di Belarus tempat kematian karena kekerasan dianggap najis, dan orang yang lewat melemparkan batu, ranting, seikat jerami, atau segenggam tanah ke tempat itu agar si mati tidak mengejar mereka.
claims.quote: В Беларуси места насильственной смерти считались нечистыми, и проходящие мимо люди на такие места бросали камни, ветки деревьев, клок соломы или горсть земли («иначе умерший будет за ними долго гнаться»).

claims.statement: Dmitry Zelenin equated the "zalozhny" dead with rusalkas.
claims.statement_id: Dmitry Zelenin menyamakan arwah "zalozhny" dengan rusalka.
claims.quote: Дмитрий Зеленин ставил знак равенства между «заложными» покойниками и русалками.

claims.statement: The upyr is a "zalozhny" dead person, most often a dead sorcerer.
claims.statement_id: Upyr adalah arwah "zalozhny", paling sering seorang dukun yang telah mati.
claims.quote: Упырь — «заложный» покойник, чаще всего умерший колдун.

claims.statement: The Ukrainian article calls Заложні мерці a collective name for beings who, in Slavic and especially Ukrainian folk belief, were people who died an unnatural death or lived a bad, unworthy life, so their souls cannot pass to the other world.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Ukraina menyebut Заложні мерці sebagai nama kolektif makhluk yang menurut kepercayaan rakyat Slavia, termasuk Ukraina, dulunya manusia yang mati tidak wajar atau hidup buruk dan tak layak, sehingga jiwanya tidak bisa pergi ke alam baka.
claims.quote: збірна назва істот, що за слов'янськими, зокрема українськими, народними повір'ями були людьми, котрі померли неприродною смертю, або які жили поганим, негідним життям, і тому їхні душі не можуть піти до потойбічного світу.

claims.statement: In many places it was believed that the earth does not accept the unclean dead: their bodies do not decay and the earth itself pushes them to the surface.
claims.statement_id: Di banyak tempat dipercaya bahwa bumi tidak menerima arwah najis: jasad mereka tidak membusuk dan bumi sendiri mendorong mereka ke permukaan.
claims.quote: В багатьох місцях вірили, що земля не приймає заложних мерців, їхні тіла не розкладаються і земля сама виштовхує їх на поверхню.

claims.statement: To stop such dead from visiting the living, a bundle of blessed poppy seed was placed in their graves, and people sprinkled their own houses with blessed poppy or flax.
claims.statement_id: Agar arwah semacam itu tidak bisa mendatangi orang hidup, ke dalam kuburnya diletakkan bungkusan biji poppy yang telah diberkati, dan rumah sendiri ditaburi poppy atau rami yang diberkati.
claims.quote: Аби позбавити таких покійників здатності відвідувати живих людей, в їхні могили клали вузлик свяченого маку-видюку. Власні ж хати обсипали свяченим маком або льоном.

claims.statement: Utqaçı (Уткучы) is a figure of the shamanic cult of the indigenous peoples of the Altai.
claims.statement_id: Utqaçı (Уткучы) adalah tokoh dalam kultus perdukunan (syamanisme) masyarakat asli Altai.
claims.quote: Уткучы — персонаж шаманского культа коренных народов Алтая.

claims.statement: Utqaçı is considered one of the heavenly spirits (spirits of the "upper" world); he serves as messenger of the supreme spirit Ülgen, lives only in the sky and never comes down to earth.
claims.statement_id: Utqaçı dianggap salah satu roh langit (roh dunia "atas"); ia berperan sebagai utusan roh tertinggi Ülgen, hanya tinggal di langit dan tidak turun ke bumi.
claims.quote: Уткучы считается одним из небесных духов (духов «верхнего» мира). Исполняет роль посланника верховного духа Ульгеня. Живёт только на небе, на землю не спускается.

claims.statement: Utqaçı met the shaman on the so-called "fifth layer of the sky", located by the Pole Star.
claims.statement_id: Pertemuan Utqaçı dengan dukun terjadi di "lapisan langit kelima" dekat Bintang Kutub.
claims.quote: Встреча происходила на так называемом «пятом слое неба», который располагался у Полярной звезды

claims.statement: Utqaçı listened to the shaman, took his sacrificial animal and led it to Ülgen with the shaman's words; returning, he announced the supreme god's will and gave the shaman geese that carried him back to earth.
claims.statement_id: Utqaçı mendengarkan dukun, mengambil hewan kurbannya dan membawanya ke Ülgen beserta pesan sang dukun; setelah kembali, ia menyampaikan kehendak dewa tertinggi dan memberi dukun angsa-angsa yang membawanya pulang ke bumi.
claims.quote: Уткучы слушал шамана, забирал у него жертвенное животное и отводил его к Ульгеню, передавая тому слова камлавшего. Возвратившись, Уткучы озвучивал волю верховного божества и давал шаману гусей, которые доставляли его на землю.

claims.statement: The Azerbaijani article calls Utqaçı Xan the god of sacrifice in Turkic and Altai mythology, also called Utkuçı, who delivers sacrifices to Ülgen.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Azerbaijan menyebut Utqaçı Xan sebagai dewa kurban dalam mitologi Turk dan Altai, juga disebut Utkuçı, yang menyampaikan kurban kepada Ülgen.
claims.quote: Utqaçı Xan - türk və altay mifologiyasında qurban ilahı. Utkuçı da deyilir. Qurbanları Ülgenə çatdırar.

claims.statement: The spirit's name literally means "the one who greets warmly".
claims.statement_id: Nama roh ini secara harfiah berarti "yang menyambut dengan ramah".
claims.quote: Буквальный перевод имени этого духа — «приветливо встречающий».

claims.statement: The Turkish article calls Utkaçı Han the God of Sacrifice in Turkic and Altai mythology.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Turki menyebut Utkaçı Han sebagai Dewa Kurban dalam mitologi Turk dan Altai.
claims.quote: Utkaçı Han - Türk ve Altay mitolojisinde Kurban Tanrısı.

claims.statement: The name derives from the root Ut and means "cheerful" or "winning".
claims.statement_id: Nama ini diturunkan dari akar Ut dan berarti "yang ramah" atau "yang menang".
claims.quote: (Ut) kökünden türemiştir. Güleryüzlü, kazanan demektir.

claims.statement: The Vadleány is a spirit being of Central European (Hungarian) folklore; like nymphs or dryads, she has extremely long hair and long fingernails and is completely nude.
claims.statement_id: Vadleány adalah makhluk roh dari cerita rakyat Eropa Tengah (Hungaria); mirip nimfa atau driad, ia berambut sangat panjang, berkuku panjang, dan sepenuhnya telanjang.
claims.quote: A Vadleány is a spiritual being from Central European (Hungarian) folklore. Similar to nymphs or dryads, Vadleány have extremely long hair, long fingernails, and are completely nude.

claims.statement: According to the Encyclopedia of Fairies in World Folklore and Mythology, vadleány seduce wanderers and steal their strength; the name means "wild girl".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Encyclopedia of Fairies in World Folklore and Mythology, vadleány menggoda para pengembara dan mencuri kekuatan mereka; namanya berarti "gadis liar".
claims.quote: According to the Encyclopedia of Fairies in World Folklore and Mythology, they seduce wanderers and steal their strength. The name translates to "wild girl".

claims.statement: When a vadleány is present, the trees rustle.
claims.statement_id: Ketika seorang vadleány hadir, pepohonan berdesir.
claims.quote: When one is present, the trees make a rustling sound.

claims.statement: The Hungarian article calls the vadleány a supernatural being of Central European, in particular Hungarian, folklore: a forest being who seduces travellers and steals their strength.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Hungaria menyebut vadleány sebagai makhluk gaib dalam folklor Eropa Tengah, khususnya Hungaria: makhluk hutan yang menggoda para pelancong dan mencuri kekuatan mereka.
claims.quote: A vadleány egy természetfeletti lény a közép-európai (azon belül a magyar) folklórban. Erdei lény, aki elcsábítja az utazókat, és ellopja az erejüket.

claims.statement: The Hungarians of Lápos (láposi magyarok) also knew the vadleány: she goes naked (meztelenül jár), her face is beautiful, but her body is covered with hair reaching to the ground.
claims.statement_id: Orang Hungaria di Lápos (láposi magyarok) juga mengenal vadleány: ia berjalan telanjang, wajahnya cantik, tetapi tubuhnya tertutup bulu yang menjuntai sampai ke tanah.
claims.quote: A vadleányt ismerték a láposi magyarok is: meztelenül jár, az arca szép, a testét azonban földig érő szőr fedi.

claims.statement: If angered she raises a wind that breaks trees and scatters the shepherd's hut; according to the people of Domokos she could be caught by setting out one boot of a pair where she usually walked.
claims.statement_id: Jika dibuat marah, ia menimbulkan angin yang mematahkan pohon dan memorakporandakan pondok gembala; menurut orang Domokos, ia bisa ditangkap dengan meletakkan sebelah sepatu bot di jalur yang biasa dilaluinya.
claims.quote: Ha felbosszantják, olyan szelet csinál, hogy fákat tör ki, széthányja a pásztor kalibáját. A domokosiak szerint meg lehetett fogni: amerre járni szokott, fél pár csizmát kellett kitenni.

claims.statement: The Hungarians of Mezőség and Székelyföld also knew this figure, calling her erdei leány (forest girl), éneklő kisasszony (singing maiden) and víg leány (merry girl).
claims.statement_id: Orang Hungaria di Mezőség dan Székelyföld juga mengenal gambaran ini dan menyebutnya erdei leány (gadis hutan), éneklő kisasszony (nona penyanyi), dan víg leány (gadis riang).
claims.quote: A képzetet ismerték a mezőségi és székelyföldi magyarok is: erdei leánynak, éneklő kisasszonynak, víg leánynak emlegették.

claims.statement: Out of curiosity she tried it on but put both feet in, and so could not run away.
claims.statement_id: Karena penasaran ia mencobanya, tetapi memasukkan kedua kakinya sehingga tidak bisa lari.
claims.quote: Kíváncsiságában felpróbálta, de mindkét lábát beledugta, így aztán nem futhatott el.

claims.statement: Vâlvă (plural vâlve) is a female spirit of Romanian folklore believed to walk over the hilltops at night; they are divided into the beneficial Vâlve Albe ("White Vâlve") and the evil Vâlve Negre ("Black Vâlve").
claims.statement_id: Vâlvă (jamak vâlve) adalah roh perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Rumania yang dipercaya berjalan di puncak-puncak bukit pada malam hari; mereka terbagi menjadi Vâlve Albe ("Vâlve Putih") yang baik dan Vâlve Negre ("Vâlve Hitam") yang jahat.
claims.quote: Vâlvă (plural vâlve) is a female spirit mentioned in the Romanian folklore. The Vâlve are believed to walk over the hilltops at night, and are subdivided into Vâlve Albe ("White Vâlve"), who are considered beneficial, and Vâlve Negre ("Black Vâlve" or "Dark Vâlve"), who are considered evil.

claims.statement: They may appear in various guises, such as shadows or black cats, and can shapeshift.
claims.statement_id: Mereka bisa muncul dalam berbagai wujud, seperti bayangan atau kucing hitam, dan mampu berubah wujud.
claims.quote: They may also appear under various guises, such as shadows or black cats. They also have the ability to shapeshift.

claims.statement: Vâlva Băilor ("of the mines") is the defender and protector of mines and tunnels, whose departure means the deposit is running out. Legends of her flourish in traditional metal-mining areas of Romania.
claims.statement_id: Vâlva Băilor ("dari tambang") adalah pembela dan pelindung tambang dan terowongan; kepergiannya berarti endapan bijih akan habis. Legenda tentangnya berkembang di daerah tambang logam tradisional di Rumania.
claims.quote: Vâlva Băilor ("of the mines"), defender and protector of mines and tunnels, whose departure means that the deposit is coming to an end

claims.statement: The Russian article calls the Вылва a female spirit of Romanian mythology who roams the hilltops at night and may be good (vâlve albe, white) or evil (vâlve negre, black).
claims.statement_id: Artikel Rusia menyebut Вылва sebagai roh perempuan dalam mitologi Rumania yang berkeliaran di puncak bukit pada malam hari, dan bisa baik (vâlve albe, putih) atau jahat (vâlve negre, hitam).
claims.quote: Вылва (рум. Vâlva) — в румынской мифологии женский дух, бродящий ночью по вершинам холмов. Вылвы могут быть как добрыми (vâlve albe, белые), так и злыми (vâlve negre, чёрные).

claims.statement: Vâlva Apei is the protector of water sources and fountains.
claims.statement_id: Vâlva Apei adalah pelindung mata air dan pancuran.
claims.quote: Вылва воды (Vâlva Apei) — защитница водных источников и фонтанов.

claims.statement: Vâlve can take various forms: often women, sometimes mere shadows or black cats; they can protect a village from storm, hail and hurricane.
claims.statement_id: Vâlve bisa mengambil berbagai wujud: sering seperti perempuan, kadang hanya bayangan atau kucing hitam; mereka bisa melindungi desa dari badai, hujan es, dan angin topan.
claims.quote: Вылвы могут принимать разный облик. Часто они выглядят как женщины, иногда просто как тени или чёрные кошки. Вылвы могут защищать село от бури, града, урагана.

claims.statement: Vâlva Ciumei controls plague and other diseases.
claims.statement_id: Vâlva Ciumei menguasai wabah sampar dan penyakit lain.
claims.quote: Вылва чумы (Vâlva Ciumei) — управляет чумой и другими болезнями.

claims.statement: Vâlva Comorilor is the protector of treasures who can also show where treasure is buried.
claims.statement_id: Vâlva Comorilor adalah pelindung harta yang juga bisa menunjukkan tempat harta karun dikubur.
claims.quote: Вылва сокровищ (Vâlva Comorilor) — защитница сокровищ, которая также может указать место, где зарыт клад.

claims.statement: Vâlva Băilor is the protector of mines; when she leaves a mine, the ore is thought to be running out.
claims.statement_id: Vâlva Băilor adalah pelindung tambang; jika ia meninggalkan tambang, bijihnya dianggap akan habis.
claims.quote: Вылва руды (Vâlva Băilor) — защитница шахт; когда она покидает копь, считается, что руда заканчивается.

claims.statement: The Romanian article says vâlve are said to be children conceived on great feast days, and in rural areas such children are said to be born with a small red cap or swelling on the head.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Rumania menyebut bahwa vâlve konon adalah anak-anak yang dikandung pada hari raya besar, dan di pedesaan dikatakan anak-anak ini lahir dengan semacam topi kecil atau benjolan merah di kepala.
claims.quote: Se spune că ar fi copiii care sunt concepuți la zile mari, de sărbătoare. În zonele rurale se spune că acești copii se nasc cu o tichiuță sau cu o gogoașă pe cap, roșie

claims.statement: The solomonari are said to be Vâlve, people who are different and have special powers.
claims.statement_id: Konon para solomonar adalah Vâlve, orang-orang yang berbeda dan memiliki kekuatan istimewa.
claims.quote: Se spune despre solomonari că sunt Vâlve, că sunt oameni diferiți, având puteri deosebite.

claims.statement: Baloz or bajloz is a legendary character of Albanian mythology and folklore, an antagonist of the Albanian legendary heroes, sometimes described as a sea monster.
claims.statement_id: Baloz atau bajloz adalah tokoh legenda dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania, lawan para pahlawan legendaris Albania, dan kadang digambarkan sebagai monster laut.
claims.quote: Baloz or bajloz is a legendary character in Albanian mythology and folklore, who appears as an antagonist of the Albanian legendary heroes. He sometimes is described as a sea monster.

claims.statement: Baloz is found in many Albanian myths and legends about fighting the Albanian nobles Muji, Halili, Gjergj Elez Alia and Constantin, and in the Albanian Songs of the Frontier Warriors.
claims.statement_id: Baloz ditemukan dalam banyak mitos dan legenda Albania tentang pertarungan melawan bangsawan Albania seperti Muji, Halili, Gjergj Elez Alia, dan Constantin, serta dalam Lagu-Lagu Pejuang Perbatasan Albania.
claims.quote: Baloz (as a character) has been found in many Albanian myths and legends about fighting against the Albanian nobles such as: Muji, Halili, Gjergj Elez Alia and Constantin. The monster is found in the Albanian Songs of the Frontier Warriors.

claims.statement: The word baloz or bajloz seems to derive from the Latin baiulus.
claims.statement_id: Kata baloz atau bajloz tampaknya berasal dari kata Latin baiulus.
claims.quote: The word baloz or bajloz seems to be derived from the Latin word baiulus.

claims.statement: Maximilian Lambertz suggested that Baloz derives from the Italian bailo, the title of the Venetian ambassador to the Ottomans.
claims.statement_id: Maximilian Lambertz mengusulkan bahwa kata Baloz berasal dari kata Italia bailo, gelar duta besar Venesia untuk Utsmaniyah.
claims.quote: Maximilian Lambertz also suggested that the word 'Baloz' is derived from Italian bailo, the title of the Venetian ambassador to the Ottomans.

claims.statement: Baloz Sedelija was a Slavic warrior in Albanian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Baloz Sedelija adalah prajurit Slavia dalam cerita rakyat Albania.
claims.quote: Baloz Sedelija was a Slavic warrior in Albanian folklore.

claims.statement: Bajlozi or balozi is a mythological-demonological figure of Albanian folk rhapsodies, a danger coming from the sea; according to Arshi Pipa he is described as an evil giant and at times a monster in folk mythology.
claims.statement_id: Bajlozi atau balozi adalah tokoh mitologis-demonologis rapsodi rakyat Albania sebagai bahaya yang datang dari laut; menurut Arshi Pipa ia digambarkan sebagai raksasa jahat dan kadang monster dalam mitologi rakyat.
claims.quote: Bajlozi ose balozi është një figurë mitologjike-demonologjike e rapsodive popullore shqiptare si një rrezik të ardhur nga deti. Sipas Arshi Pipës përshkruhet si një vigan i keq, herë-herë, përbindësh në mitologjinë popullore.

claims.statement: Its root, Latin baiulus, means overseer or keeper.
claims.statement_id: Akar katanya, baiulus dalam bahasa Latin, berarti pengawas atau pemelihara.
claims.quote: Në rrënjën e vet baiulus në gjuhën latine do të thotë mbikëqyrës, mbarështues

claims.statement: Historically, the figure relates to the demonisation of the Republic of Saint Mark (Venice).
claims.statement_id: Secara historis, tokoh ini berkaitan dengan demonisasi Republik Santo Markus (Venesia).
claims.quote: Në rrafshin historik ka të bëjë me demonizimin e Republikës së Shën Markut

claims.statement: Gjergj Elez Alia fought the bajloz who came from the sea and defeated him, though he had just come through a long illness from nine war wounds.
claims.statement_id: Gjergj Elez Alia melawan bajloz yang datang dari laut dan mengalahkannya walaupun baru pulih dari sakit panjang akibat sembilan luka perang.
claims.quote: Gjergj Elez Alia luftoi me bajlozin e ardhur nga deti, duke e mundur atë edhe pse vinte pas një lëngate te gjate për shkak te nënte plagëve te marra ne lufte.

claims.statement: A bardha ("the white one") is an Albanian mythological figure appearing as a zana (nymph) or an ora (Fate goddess) associated with good luck; the plural is bardhat.
claims.statement_id: Bardha (bahasa Inggris "the white one", yang putih) adalah tokoh mitologi Albania yang tampil sebagai zana (nimfa) atau ora (dewi takdir) yang terkait keberuntungan; bentuk jamaknya bardhat.
claims.quote: A bardha (Albanian pronunciation: [baɾða], English: 'the white one') is an Albanian mythological figure, appearing either as a zana (nymph) or as an ora (Fate goddess) associated with good luck. The plural form is bardhat.

claims.statement: Bardhat are described as pale, nebulous figures or apparitions of women in white living on misty mountains and in the underworld; they are sometimes considered mountain or nature spirits.
claims.statement_id: Bardhat digambarkan sebagai sosok pucat berkabut atau penampakan perempuan berbaju putih yang tinggal di gunung berkabut dan di dunia bawah; kadang dianggap roh gunung atau roh alam.
claims.quote: Bardhat are described as pale, nebulous figures, or as apparitions of women in white that live both on misty mountains and in the underworld. They are sometimes considered mountain or nature spirits.

claims.statement: They are generally indifferent to humans but harm those who offend them, can paralyse or mute a person who accidentally steps on them, and make a rider fall if the horse steps on them.
claims.statement_id: Mereka umumnya tidak peduli pada manusia tetapi mencelakai orang yang menyinggungnya, dapat membuat lumpuh atau bisu orang yang tak sengaja menginjaknya, dan membuat penunggang jatuh bila kudanya menginjak mereka.
claims.quote: They are generally indifferent to humans, but will harm people if offended, and can paralyze or make mute a person who inadvertently steps on them. It is also said that they cause the rider of a horse to fall off if the horse steps on them.

claims.statement: To appease them, especially after an accident, people would leave sugar, cakes or honey on the ground at the spot and say nice things about the bardha.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menenangkan mereka, terutama setelah kecelakaan, orang meninggalkan gula, kue, atau madu di tanah tempat kejadian dan memuji bardha.
claims.quote: In order to appease them, especially after an accident, one would leave sugar, cakes, or honey on the ground at the site where it happened and say nice things about the bardha.

claims.statement: The inhabitants of the Dukagjini Mountains believed in three types of Ora: e Bardha (The White One) gives good luck, e Verdha (The Yellow One) bad luck and evil spells, and e Zeza (The Black One) decides death.
claims.statement_id: Penduduk Pegunungan Dukagjini percaya ada tiga jenis Ora: e Bardha (Yang Putih) membagikan keberuntungan, e Verdha (Yang Kuning) membagikan nasib buruk dan mantra jahat, dan e Zeza (Yang Hitam) menentukan kematian.
claims.quote: The inhabitants of the Dukagjini Mountains believed that three types of Ora (Fate goddesses) existed: "e Bardha (The White One) distributes good luck and wishes humans well, e Verdha (The Yellow One) distributes bad luck and casts evil spells, and e Zeza (The Black One) who decides death".

claims.statement: According to old folklore that sees them as nymph-like, a bardha is similar to zana e malit.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita rakyat lama yang menganggap mereka mirip nimfa, bardha serupa dengan zana e malit.
claims.quote: According to old folklore that thinks of them as nymph-like creatures, a bardha is similar to zana e malit.

claims.statement: According to Albanian folk belief they are pale, misty figures who live underground.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Albania, mereka adalah sosok pucat berkabut yang tinggal di bawah tanah.
claims.quote: Sipas besimit popullor shqiptar ato janë figura të zbehta, të mjegullta që banojnë nën tokë.

claims.statement: Chudo-Yudo ("sea wonder") is a Russian folk-tale character often with fish traits; ethnographers and cultural scholars have not agreed on its origin.
claims.statement_id: Chudo-Yudo (Чудо-юдо, "keajaiban laut") adalah tokoh dongeng rakyat Rusia yang sering berciri ikan; etnografer dan ahli budaya belum sepakat tentang asal-usulnya.
claims.quote: Чудо-юдо (чудо морское) — персонаж русских народных сказок, часто обладающий чертами и свойствами рыбы. Единого мнения о происхождении персонажа в работах этнографов и культурологов на сегодняшний день не сложилось.

claims.statement: According to A. N. Afanasyev, in other versions of the tale of the Sea King and his wise daughter the Sea King's role passes to a serpent, the devil and the lawless Chudo-Yudo.
claims.statement_id: Menurut A. N. Afanasyev, dalam versi lain dongeng Raja Laut dan putrinya yang bijak, peran Raja Laut diberikan kepada ular, setan, dan Chudo-Yudo yang durjana.
claims.quote: в одном варианте народной сказки о Морском Царе и его вещей дочери Морской Царь прямо назван Окиан-море; в других же списках роль его передаётся змею, чёрту и беззаконному Чуду-Юду.

claims.statement: According to Afanasyev, the name Chudo-Yudo is mostly given to the mythical serpent, the dragon-cloud.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Afanasyev, nama Chudo-Yudo kebanyakan diberikan kepada ular mitis, yaitu naga-awan.
claims.quote: Название Чудо-Юдо, согласно Афанасьеву, подтверждает ту же мысль: оно большею частью придаётся мифическому змею (дракону-туче).

claims.statement: Max Vasmer thought it most likely that "yudo" is merely a rhyming formation modelled on "chudo".
claims.statement_id: Max Vasmer menganggap paling mungkin bahwa "yudo" hanyalah bentukan berima dari kata "chudo".
claims.quote: Макс Фасмер считал наиболее вероятным, что юдо — «всего лишь рифмованное образование по образцу слова чудо»

claims.statement: In the tale "Ivan the Peasant's Son and Chudo-Yudo", Chudo-Yudo is a group of evil 6-, 9- and 12-headed serpents living beyond the River Smorodina, crossing by the Kalinov Bridge, shown on horseback, burning towns and villages.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng "Ivan, Anak Petani, dan Chudo-Yudo", Chudo-Yudo adalah sekelompok ular berkepala 6, 9, dan 12 (enam, sembilan, dua belas) yang jahat, tinggal di seberang Sungai Smorodina dan menyeberang lewat Jembatan Kalinov, digambarkan menunggang kuda, dan membakar kota serta desa.
claims.quote: В русской народной сказке «Иван — крестьянский сын и Чудо-юдо» Чудо-юдо — это группа многоголовых (6-, 9-, 12-головых) змеев, отрицательных персонажей. Живут они за рекой Смородиной, через которую перебираются по Калинову мосту. В сказке Чудо-юдо изображается верхом на коне. Вред от него заключается в том, что оно сжигает города-сёла огнём.

claims.statement: The 12-headed (twelve-headed) Chudo-Yudo has a fiery finger that regrows severed heads.
claims.statement_id: Chudo-Yudo berkepala 12 (dua belas) punya jari berapi yang dapat menumbuhkan kembali kepala yang terpenggal.
claims.quote: 12-головое Чудо-юдо обладает огненным пальцем, который позволяет регенерировать срубленные головы.

claims.statement: Chudo-Yudo lives in stone chambers with sorceress wives and a serpent mother; its chief opponent is Ivan, the peasant's son.
claims.statement_id: Chudo-Yudo tinggal di istana batu bersama istri-istri penyihir dan ibu ularnya; lawan utamanya adalah Ivan, anak petani.
claims.quote: Живёт чудо-юдо в каменных палатах, где у чуда-юда есть жёны-колдуньи и мать-змеиха. Главный противник чуда-юда, как и следует из названия сказки, — Иван — крестьянский сын.

claims.statement: In Pyotr Yershov's 1834 tale "Конёк-Горбунок" (The Little Humpbacked Horse), Chudo-Yudo the Fish-Whale appears as a separate character, an island-fish lying across the sea.
claims.statement_id: Dalam dongeng Pyotr Yershov "Конёк-Горбунок" (Kuda Kecil Bungkuk) tahun 1834, Chudo-Yudo Ikan-Paus tampil sebagai tokoh tersendiri, yaitu ikan-pulau yang berbaring melintang di laut.
claims.quote: В сказке Петра Ершова «Конёк-Горбунок» 1834 года как самостоятельный персонаж присутствует Чудо-юдо Рыба-кит. Собственно, это рыба-остров, которая лежит «поперёк моря».

claims.statement: Chudo-Yudo is a character of Russian folk tales.
claims.statement_id: Chudo-Yudo adalah tokoh dongeng rakyat Rusia.
claims.quote: Чудо-юдо — рус халыҡ әкиәттәре персонажы.

claims.statement: Djall or Dreq is the personification of evil in Albanian mythology and folklore; the name is also used for a demon of fire.
claims.statement_id: Djall atau Dreq adalah personifikasi kejahatan dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania; nama ini juga dipakai untuk iblis api.
claims.quote: Djall or Dreq is the personification of evil in Albanian mythology and folklore. The name is used also for a demon of fire.

claims.statement: Various tales have cast Djall as the antagonist that heroes and ordinary people alike must contend with.
claims.statement_id: Berbagai kisah menempatkan Djall sebagai tokoh jahat yang harus dilawan para pahlawan maupun orang biasa.
claims.quote: Various tales woven through the years have pitched Djall as the antagonist, the villainous element against which heroes and ordinary people alike must contend.

claims.statement: The name djall derives from Latin diabolus, "devil"; alternative forms are dreqi from Latin draco, "dragon", satan and shejtan.
claims.statement_id: Nama djall berasal dari kata Latin diabolus, "iblis"; bentuk lainnya dreqi dari Latin draco, "naga", serta satan dan shejtan.
claims.quote: The name djall derives from the Latin diabolus, "devil". Alternative forms are dreqi from the Latin draco, "dragon", satan and shejtan.

claims.statement: Djall is no mere metaphor; in these narratives he can manifest in the physical world, most terrifyingly as a fire demon.
claims.statement_id: Djall bukan sekadar metafora; dalam kisah-kisah ini ia dapat menjelma di dunia fisik, paling menakutkan sebagai iblis api.
claims.quote: But Djall is no mere metaphor, in these narratives, it takes a form that can manifest in the physical world, most terrifyingly as a fire demon.

claims.statement: A moving inferno, he brings moral and mortal danger.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai neraka yang bergerak, ia membawa bahaya moral dan maut.
claims.quote: Një infern në lëvizje, ai sjell rrezik moral dhe vdekjeprurës.

claims.statement: Djalli or Dreqi is the personification of evil in Albanian mythology and folklore; the name is also used for a fire demon.
claims.statement_id: Djalli atau Dreqi adalah personifikasi kejahatan dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania; nama ini juga dipakai untuk iblis api.
claims.quote: Djalli ose Dreqi është personifikimi i së keqes në mitologjinë dhe folklorin shqiptar. Emri përdoret gjithashtu për një demon të zjarrit.

claims.statement: The drangue is a semi-human winged divine hero of Albanian pagan mythology tied to weather and storms; archetype of light and good opposing the kulshedra; babies destined to be drangue are born with a caul and two or four wings under the arms.
claims.statement_id: Drangue adalah pahlawan ilahi bersayap setengah manusia dalam mitologi pagan Albania, terkait cuaca dan badai; ia arketipe terang dan kebaikan, lawan kulshedra; bayi calon drangue lahir dengan kepala tertutup selaput ketuban dan dua atau empat sayap di bawah lengan.
claims.quote: is a semi-human winged divine hero in Albanian pagan mythology, associated with weather and storms. He is the archetype of light and good, the complementary and opposing force to kulshedra, the archetype of darkness and evil. Babies destined to become drangue are born with their heads covered in caul and with two or sometimes four wings under their arms.

claims.statement: To defeat the kulshedra he uses lightning-swords and thunderbolts, plus meteoric stones, piles of trees and rocks, protecting mankind from storms, fire, drought and floods caused by the kulshedra.
claims.statement_id: Untuk mengalahkan kulshedra ia memakai pedang petir dan halilintar, juga batu meteor, tumpukan pohon, dan batu, sehingga melindungi manusia dari badai, kebakaran, kekeringan, dan banjir akibat kulshedra.
claims.quote: In order to defeat the kulshedra he uses lightning-swords and thunderbolts as his most powerful weapons, but he also uses meteoric stones, piles of trees and rocks, eventually protecting mankind from storms, fire, droughts, floods and other natural disasters caused by kulshedra's destructive power.

claims.statement: The standard form is dragùa; drangue is a common dialectal variant, and Durham recorded the form drangoni.
claims.statement_id: Bentuk baku namanya dragùa; varian dialek yang umum drangue, dan Durham mencatat bentuk drangoni.
claims.quote: Standard Albanian form of the name is dragùa (def. dragói). A common dialectal variant is drangue. Durham recorded the form drangoni.

claims.statement: The sense of dragùa as a hero battling the kulshedra is attested in 17th-century Albanian texts such as the 1635 Dictionarium Latino-Epiroticum by Frang Bardhi.
claims.statement_id: Makna dragùa sebagai pahlawan yang melawan kulshedra sudah tercatat dalam teks Albania abad ke-17, seperti Dictionarium Latino-Epiroticum tahun 1635 karya Frang Bardhi.
claims.quote: a hero battling the Kulshedra, a mythological tradition already attested in the 17th century Albanian texts, such as the 1635 Dictionarium Latino-Epiroticum by Frang Bardhi.

claims.statement: Drangues are semi-human divine warriors of extraordinary strength who can uproot trees and hurl boulders, lightning bolts, meteors or whole houses.
claims.statement_id: Drangue adalah prajurit ilahi setengah manusia berkekuatan luar biasa yang dapat mencabut pohon, melempar batu besar, petir, meteor, bahkan rumah.
claims.quote: The drangues are semi-human divine warriors with extraordinary strength, giving them the ability to tear trees out of the ground and throw large boulders at their enemies. They can also cast lightning bolts and meteors, or whole houses.

claims.statement: The wings and arms of a dragùa are thought to be the source of his power.
claims.statement_id: Sayap dan lengan dragùa dianggap sumber kekuatannya.
claims.quote: The wings and arms of a dragùa are thought to be the source of his power

claims.statement: Thunderstorms are conceived as battles between drangues and kulshedras, the thunder being their weapons clashing.
claims.statement_id: Badai petir dibayangkan sebagai pertempuran drangue dan kulshedra; gemuruh guntur dianggap bunyi senjata mereka beradu.
claims.quote: Thunderstorms are conceived as battles between the drangues and the kulshedras, the roll of thunder taken to be the sounds of their weapons clashing.

claims.statement: In some parts of Kosovo such as Rugova it is believed drangues die when seen by anyone other than their mothers.
claims.statement_id: Di beberapa bagian Kosovo seperti Rugova dipercaya bahwa drangue mati bila dilihat orang selain ibunya.
claims.quote: However in some parts of Kosovo, such as Rugova it is believed that drangue's die when they are seen by somebody other than their mothers.

claims.statement: Drangue is the most widespread culture hero among Albanians.
claims.statement_id: Drangue adalah pahlawan budaya yang paling luas dikenal di kalangan orang Albania.
claims.quote: Drangue is the most widespread culture hero among Albanians.

claims.statement: The best-known Albanian mythological image of the struggle between good and evil, light and darkness, is the constant battle of drangue and kulshedra, symbolising cosmic renewal.
claims.statement_id: Gambaran mitologis Albania yang paling terkenal tentang perjuangan baik dan jahat, terang dan gelap, adalah pertarungan abadi drangue dan kulshedra, yang melambangkan pembaruan kosmis.
