claims.quote: The most famous Albanian mythological representation of the dualistic struggle between good and evil, light and darkness, is the constant battle between drangue and kulshedra, a conflict that symbolises the cyclic return in the watery and chthonian world of death, accomplishing the cosmic renewal of rebirth.

claims.statement: In the southeastern Albanian regions of Pogradec and Korça, the dragùa is envisaged as a beautiful strong winged horse defending civilisation and mankind.
claims.statement_id: Di wilayah Pogradec dan Korça di Albania tenggara, dragùa dibayangkan sebagai kuda bersayap yang indah dan kuat yang membela peradaban dan umat manusia.
claims.quote: In southeastern Albanian regions of Pogradec and Korça, the dragùa is "envisaged.. as a beautiful strong horse with wings, who defends civilization and mankind".

claims.statement: According to local lore of central Albania, he knocked her out with trees and boulders and then drowned her in the Shkumbin River.
claims.statement_id: Menurut cerita setempat di Albania tengah, drangue membuat kulshedra pingsan dengan lemparan pohon dan batu besar, lalu menenggelamkannya di Sungai Shkumbin.
claims.quote: having knocked her unconscious by throwing trees and boulders at her, and afterwards drowning her in the Shkumbin River, according to the localized lore of central Albania.

claims.statement: The celestial divine heroes who defeat the kulshedra are often drangue, but also E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit ("the Daughter of the Moon and the Sun").
claims.statement_id: Pahlawan ilahi langit yang mengalahkan kulshedra sering adalah drangue, tetapi juga E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit ("Putri Bulan dan Matahari").
claims.quote: Those celestial divine heroes are often drangue (the most widespread culture hero among Albanians), but also E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit ("the Daughter of the Moon and the Sun")

claims.statement: Drangoi or drangùe is a semi-human winged divine figure in Albanian mythology and folklore, tied to weather and storms.
claims.statement_id: Drangoi atau drangùe adalah sosok ilahi bersayap setengah manusia dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania, terkait cuaca dan badai.
claims.quote: Drangoi ose drangùe është një figurë hyjnore me krahë gjysmë-njerëzore në mitologjinë dhe folklorin shqiptar, e lidhur me motin dhe stuhitë.

claims.statement: Dzedka (Belarusian Дзедка, Russian Кладенец, Polish Skarbnik) is a character of Belarusian mythology, a good mythological creature considered a symbol of richness and companion of fortune.
claims.statement_id: Dzedka (Belarus: Дзедка, Rusia: Кладенец, Polandia: Skarbnik) adalah tokoh mitologi Belarus, makhluk mitologis yang baik, dianggap lambang kekayaan dan pendamping keberuntungan.
claims.quote: Dzedka (Belarusian: Дзедка, Russian: Кладенец, Polish: Skarbnik) is a character of Belarusian mythology. Dzedka is a good mythological creature. It is considered to be the symbol of richness and fortune companion.

claims.statement: Dzedka is described as an old man with a long red beard and red eyes, in simple clothes, looking like a beggar with a bag.
claims.statement_id: Dzedka digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua berjanggut merah panjang dan bermata merah, berpakaian sederhana, mirip pengemis yang membawa karung.
claims.quote: Dzedka is described as an old man with long red beard and red eyes. Dzedka wears simple clothes and looks like a beggar with a bag.

claims.statement: According to Belarusian folk belief, by day Dzedka walks the roads and fields; a person meeting him falls asleep before noticing him and on waking finds a desired sum of money.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat Belarus, pada siang hari Dzedka berjalan di jalan dan ladang; orang yang bertemu dengannya tertidur sebelum menyadarinya, dan saat bangun menemukan sejumlah uang yang diinginkan.
claims.quote: According to Belarusian folk beliefs, in the daytime Dzedka walks around the roads and fields. When a person meets Dzedka, prior to noticing it, this person falls asleep. When the person wakes up, he or she discovers a desired sum of money.

claims.statement: If rich but unhappy people meet Dzedka, he shows them in a dream what they must do to become happy.
claims.statement_id: Bila orang kaya yang tidak bahagia bertemu Dzedka, ia menunjukkan dalam mimpi apa yang harus mereka lakukan agar bahagia.
claims.quote: If rich, but unhappy people meet Dzedka, it shows such people in a dream what they need to do to become happy.

claims.statement: By day Dzedka walks the roads and fields; when someone meets him, Dzedka puts them to sleep before they realise it.
claims.statement_id: Pada siang hari Dzedka berjalan di jalan dan ladang; ketika seseorang bertemu dengannya, Dzedka membuatnya tertidur sebelum ia menyadarinya.
claims.quote: Pendant la journée, Dzedka se promène sur les routes et dans les champs. Lorsqu'une personne rencontre Dzedka, celui ci l'endort avant qu'elle ne s'en rende compte.

claims.statement: Dzedka is described as an old man with a long red beard and red eyes, in simple clothes, resembling a beggar with a bag.
claims.statement_id: Dzedka digambarkan sebagai lelaki tua berjanggut merah panjang dan bermata merah, berpakaian sederhana dan mirip pengemis dengan karung.
claims.quote: Dzedka est décrit comme un vieil homme ayant une longue barbe rousse et des yeux rouges. Il porte des vêtements simples et ressemble à un mendiant avec un sac.

claims.statement: She is a character of Albanian mythology and folklore, daughter of Hëna (the Moon) and Dielli (the Sun), described as pika e qiellit ("drop of the sky" or "lightning") that falls from heaven on mountains and valleys and strikes pride and evil.
claims.statement_id: Ia adalah tokoh mitologi dan cerita rakyat Albania, putri Hëna (Bulan) dan Dielli (Matahari), digambarkan sebagai pika e qiellit ("tetes langit" atau "petir") yang jatuh dari langit di gunung dan lembah serta menghantam kesombongan dan kejahatan.
claims.quote: is a character in Albanian mythology and folklore, the daughter of Hëna ("the Moon") and Dielli ("the Sun"). She is described as pika e qiellit ("drop of the sky" or "lightning") which falls everywhere from heaven on the mountains and the valleys and strikes pride and evil.

claims.statement: In Albanian folk belief the sun (Dielli) and the moon (Hëna) are personified deities; the sun appears as a male figure and the moon as a female one.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Albania, matahari (Dielli) dan bulan (Hëna) adalah dewa yang dipersonifikasikan; matahari tampil sebagai laki-laki dan bulan sebagai perempuan.
claims.quote: In Albanian folk beliefs the sun (Dielli) and the moon (Hëna) are personified deities. In folk tales, myths and legends the sun appears as a male figure, and the moon as a female figure.

claims.statement: Some traditions regard sun and moon as husband and wife, others as brother and sister; for E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit the sun is her father and the moon her mother.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sebagian tradisi matahari dan bulan dianggap suami-istri, dalam tradisi lain kakak-adik; dalam kisah E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit, matahari adalah ayahnya dan bulan ibunya.
claims.quote: In some traditions the sun and the moon are regarded as husband and wife, and in other traditions as brother and sister. In the case of E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit the sun is her father and the moon is her mother.

claims.statement: Her victory over the kulshedra symbolises the supremacy of the sky deity over the underworld deity in the dualistic struggle of light and darkness.
claims.statement_id: Kemenangannya atas kulshedra melambangkan keunggulan dewa langit atas dewa dunia bawah dalam pertarungan dualistis terang dan gelap.
claims.quote: Her victory over the kulshedra symbolizes the supremacy of the deity of the sky over that of the underworld in the dualistic struggle between light and darkness.

claims.statement: In the legends she helps a hero fight a kulshedra, an earthly or chthonic deity or demon from darkness; in Albanian mythology the kulshedra is usually defeated by the drangue, a sky and lightning divine hero.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda ia membantu seorang pahlawan melawan kulshedra, dewa atau iblis bumi yang berasal dari kegelapan; dalam mitologi Albania kulshedra biasanya dikalahkan oleh drangue, pahlawan ilahi langit dan petir.
claims.quote: In the legends she helps a hero in his fight against a kulshedra, an earthly/chthonic deity or demon originating from darkness. In Albanian mythology the kulshedra is usually fought and defeated by the drangue, also seen as a sky and lightning deity or divine hero.

claims.statement: The legend was also narrated by Albanian writer Mitrush Kuteli in the collection Tregime të moçme shqiptare ("Old Albanian tales"), published in 1965.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini juga dituturkan penulis Albania Mitrush Kuteli dalam kumpulan Tregime të moçme shqiptare ("Cerita Albania Lama") yang terbit tahun 1965.
claims.quote: The legend of E Bija e Hënës dhe e Diellit has also been narrated by the Albanian writer Mitrush Kuteli in the collection Tregime të moçme shqiptare ("Old Albanian tales"), published in 1965.

claims.statement: In the legends she helps a hero to victory over a kuçedra (kulshedra).
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda ia membantu seorang pahlawan meraih kemenangan atas kuçedra (kulshedra).
claims.quote: Në legjendat ajo ndihmon një hero në fitoren e tij kundër një kuçedre.

claims.statement: Ebajalg (whirlwind) is a being of Estonian mythology, a whirlwind believed to be a malicious spirit or demon, described as very strong and often destructive.
claims.statement_id: Ebajalg (angin puting) adalah makhluk dalam mitologi Estonia, berupa pusaran angin yang dipercaya sebagai roh atau iblis jahat; digambarkan sangat kuat dan sering merusak.
claims.quote: Ebajalg (whirlwind) is a being found in Estonian mythology. It is a whirlwind, believed to be a malicious spirit or demon. They are described as having great strength, often leading to destruction.

claims.statement: Tuulispask (also vihur or ebajalg) is the folk name for a strong whirlwind moving over land.
claims.statement_id: Tuulispask (juga vihur atau ebajalg) adalah nama rakyat untuk pusaran angin kuat yang bergerak di atas daratan.
claims.quote: Tuulispask (ka vihur või ebajalg) on rahvapärane nimetus maismaa kohal liikuva tugeva tuulekeerise kohta.

claims.statement: In Estonian folk belief the whirlwind was commonly imagined to be caused by the soul of a person (a witch) temporarily out of the body, more rarely the soul of a dead person.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Estonia lazim dibayangkan bahwa pusaran angin ditimbulkan jiwa manusia (penyihir) yang sementara meninggalkan tubuhnya, lebih jarang jiwa orang mati.
claims.quote: Eesti rahvausundis oli levinud kujutelm, et keeristuult tekitab inimese(nõia) kehast ajutiselt lahkunud hing, harvem surnud inimese hing.

claims.statement: The whirlwind could also be a being made or sent by a witch; among the Seto it was the devil, his son or mother; it carried off grain and hay from others' fields, also luck, brought illness and did other harm.
claims.statement_id: Pusaran angin juga bisa makhluk yang dibuat atau dikirim penyihir; di kalangan Seto ia iblis, anaknya, atau ibunya; ia membawa pergi gandum dan jerami dari ladang orang lain, juga keberuntungan, membawa penyakit, dan berbuat jahat lainnya.
claims.quote: Tuulispask võis olla ka nõia tehtud või saadetud olevus, setudel kurat, selle poeg või ema. Uskumuse järgi viis ta võõrastelt põldudelt ära vilja, heina jms, kuid võis ära viia ka õnne, tuua haigust ja teha muud halba.

claims.statement: According to Matthias Johann Eisen, in the south the tuulispask is also called ebajalg; the ebajalg shows great strength, even carrying off haystacks.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Matthias Johann Eisen, di selatan tuulispask disebut juga ebajalg; ebajalg menunjukkan kekuatan sangat besar, bahkan membawa pergi tumpukan jerami.
claims.quote: Lõuna pool nimetatakse tuulispaska ka ebajalaks. Ebajalg avaldab iseäranis suurt jõudu, viib isegi heinasaod ja -kuhjad kaasa.

claims.statement: The whirlwind was warded off magically; a common method was to throw a bladed tool into it, hoping that hitting the soul would also wound the person's body.
claims.statement_id: Pusaran angin ditangkal dengan cara magis; cara yang sering dipakai adalah melempar benda tajam ke pusaran, berharap jiwa yang terkena membuat tubuh orang itu ikut terluka.
claims.quote: Tuulispaska tõrjuti maagiliste võtetega. Sageli kasutatud võte oli visata keerist mõne terariistaga, lootes, et nii hinge tabades saab vigastatud ka vastava isiku keha.

claims.statement: Faronika is a fish or water serpent of Slovene folklore that carries the earth on its back; its movement causes earthquakes, and when it dives the world ends.
claims.statement_id: Faronika adalah ikan atau ular air dalam cerita rakyat Slovenia yang memikul bumi di punggungnya; geraknya menyebabkan gempa, dan bila ia menyelam dunia berakhir.
claims.quote: Faronika je ryba či vodní had ze slovinského folklóru, která na svých zádech nese zemi. Její pohyb způsobuje zemětřesení a když se potopí nastane konec světa.

claims.statement: A fish or serpent linked to the cosmic ocean is a common motif of many mythical cosmologies, such as the biblical Leviathan or the Norse Jörmungandr.
claims.statement_id: Ikan atau ular yang terkait samudra kosmis adalah motif umum banyak kosmologi mitis, misalnya Leviatan dalam Alkitab atau Jörmungandr dalam mitologi Nordik.
claims.quote: Ryba či had spojený s kosmickým oceánem je běžným motivem mnoha mytických kosmologií, příkladem je biblický Leviatan nebo severský Jörmungandr

claims.statement: Its name derives from the biblical Pharaoh who drowned in the Red Sea and, according to Slovene folk belief, turned into a fish.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berasal dari Firaun dalam Alkitab yang tenggelam di Laut Merah dan, menurut kepercayaan rakyat Slovenia, berubah menjadi ikan.
claims.quote: Její jméno je odvozeno od biblického faraóna, který utonul v Rudém moři, a podle slovinské lidové víry se změnil v rybu.

claims.statement: Faronika is a figure of Slovene mythology, a fish-shaped being that carries the world on its back.
claims.statement_id: Faronika adalah tokoh mitologi Slovenia, makhluk berbentuk ikan yang memikul dunia di punggungnya.
claims.quote: Faronika je lik iz slovenske mitologije. Je bitje v obliki ribe, ki na hrbtu nosi svet.

claims.statement: Slovenes from Zámuří instead know two fish circling the earth in the waters, causing earthquakes when they rub against it or strike it with their tails.
claims.statement_id: Orang Slovenia dari Zámuří justru mengenal dua ikan yang berputar di air mengelilingi bumi dan menimbulkan gempa saat menggesek atau memukulnya dengan ekor.
claims.quote: Slovinci ze Zámuří znají naopak ryby dvě, které kolem země krouží na vodách, a když se o ní otřou či ji zasáhnou svým ocasem způsobí zemětřesení.

claims.statement: The Faronika tale later merged with the legend of Veronika of Mali Grad near Kamnik, turned into half woman, half snake for her greed.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Faronika kemudian bercampur dengan legenda Veronika dari Mali Grad dekat Kamnik, yang karena ketamakannya diubah menjadi setengah perempuan setengah ular.
claims.quote: Příběh o Faronice později splynul s pověstí o Veronice z Mali Gradu u Kamniku, která byla kvůli své lakotě proměněna v napůl ženu, napůl hada.

claims.statement: The fish Faronika, as a mythological being, is said to appear in an Old Slavic, Christian-linked story of the creation of the world, in which at first only God, the Sun and the sea existed.
claims.statement_id: Ikan Faronika, sebagai makhluk mitologis, konon muncul dalam kisah Slavia lama terkait Kekristenan tentang penciptaan dunia, ketika yang ada hanyalah Tuhan, Matahari, dan laut.
claims.quote: Riba Faronika, naj bi, kot mitološko bitje, nastopala v s krščanstvom povezani staroslovanski zgodbi o nastanku sveta, v katerem so sprva obstajali le Bog, Sonce in morje.

claims.statement: Gundyr is a many-headed giant of Komi mythology; in Komi-Zyrian and Komi-Permyak folklore he had human form but under Russian folklore influence became a giant serpent or dragon.
claims.statement_id: Gundyr (Гундыр) adalah raksasa berkepala banyak dalam mitologi Komi; dalam cerita rakyat Komi-Zyrian dan Komi-Permyak ia berwujud manusia, tetapi di bawah pengaruh cerita rakyat Rusia berubah menjadi ular atau naga raksasa.
claims.quote: Гундыр — образ многоголового великана в мифологии коми. В фольклоре коми-зырян и коми-пермяков Гундыр имел человеческий образ, однако под влиянием русского фольклора превратился в гигантского змея или дракона.

claims.statement: Tales disagree on the number of his heads: 3, 6, 9, 12 or even 24 (three, six, nine, twelve, twenty-four).
claims.statement_id: Dongeng dan cerita tidak sepakat tentang jumlah kepalanya: bisa 3, 6, 9, 12, atau bahkan 24 (tiga, enam, sembilan, dua belas, dua puluh empat).
claims.quote: По сказкам и быличкам нет однозначного ответа о количестве его голов; их может быть 3, 6, 9, 12 или даже 24.

claims.statement: His breath is considered pezh, unclean; in tales he lives under water, underground, in or on a mountain, or in the sky, and emerges as a black cloud, black smoke or blue mist.
claims.statement_id: Napasnya dianggap pezh, najis; dalam berbagai cerita ia tinggal di bawah air, di bawah tanah, di dalam atau di atas gunung, atau di langit, dan keluar sebagai awan hitam, asap hitam, atau kabut biru.
claims.quote: Дыхание его считается пеж — нечистым. Обитает он в различных быличках под водой, землёй, в горе или на ней, либо на небе. Выходит он из своего укрытия в виде чёрной тучи, чёрного дыма или синего тумана.

claims.statement: He is a negative figure in Komi mythology and in fairy tales is always the hero's opponent.
claims.statement_id: Ia tokoh negatif dalam mitologi Komi dan dalam dongeng selalu menjadi lawan tokoh utama.
claims.quote: Является отрицательным персонажем в мифологии коми. В сказках выступает всегда как противник главного героя.

claims.statement: He is often called master of a lake, sea or mountain; guards magical wealth or an object; devours people and Shondi (the Sun), abducts wives and brides; and is often husband, son or son-in-law of Yoma.
claims.statement_id: Ia sering disebut penguasa danau, laut, atau gunung; menjaga harta atau benda ajaib; memangsa manusia dan Shondi (Matahari), menculik istri dan tunangan orang; sering menjadi suami, anak, atau menantu Yoma.
claims.quote: Его часто называли хозяином определённого места: озера, моря, горы. Сюжет сказок часто завязан на том, что он сторожит волшебное богатство или предмет. Пожирает людей, Шонды, похищает чужих жён и невест. Часто сам является мужем, сыном или зятем Йомы.

claims.statement: Gundyr is a beast-and-human-like figure with 4, 6, 9 or 12 heads, a tail and iron skin, living under water, on and under the earth, and travelling by horse cart; his role is close to the Russian Zmey Gorynych.
claims.statement_id: Gundyr adalah tokoh mirip hewan dan manusia, berkepala 4, 6, 9, atau 12, berekor, berkulit besi, tinggal di bawah air, di atas dan di bawah tanah, dan bepergian dengan kereta kuda; fungsinya dekat dengan Zmey Gorynych Rusia.
claims.quote: Гундыр – пемӧс да морт кодь персонаж. Сiйӧ: 4, 6, 9, 12 юра, бӧжа, кӧрт кучика, олӧ ва улын, му вылын да му улын, ветлӧ вӧла телегаӧн. ... Функция серти матын роч Змей Горынычлы
